5.title: DRAM — Manchurius Hao
5.body:
The memory investment depends more on near-term earnings than on interest-rate forecasts.

Low forward earnings multiples make it less reliant on profits far in the future, provided demand and margins hold up.

6.title: EOSE / GOOG — Manchurius Hao
6.body:
Eos Energy offers a potential turnaround if factory improvements lead to dependable deliveries. Manufacturing problems, cash burn and heavy losses remain obstacles.

Linked ChatGPT research suggests a path to resolving the operational problems and a reported opportunity with Google. The case depends on actual improvement; a turnaround can still fail.

7.title: BE — Manchurius Hao
7.body: Bloom Energy is the top pick as data centers face growing pressure to generate their own electricity.

8.title: SNOW — Manchurius Hao
8.body: Snowflake broke higher after holding around $280 for roughly a month without filling an earlier price gap. The setup anticipates strength over the following two weeks, with a $280 stop.

9.title: EQNR / CVX / XOM / VIST — Manchurius Hao
9.body:
Chevron and Exxon remain the large-cap oil benchmarks, while Equinor and Vista Energy offer more specific exposure outside the conflict zone.

Equinor sells oil, refining products and gas delivered directly to Europe. Vista produces shale oil in Argentina; Peter Thiel's investment adds interest, but Argentine policy is the main risk.

media.alt: EQNR / CVX / XOM / VIST quoted source chart

10.title: 000660.KS — Art of Speculation
10.body:
SK Hynix's quarterly revenue and profit missed expectations, but long-term demand guidance remained intact.

The miss raises near-term concerns while demand is still expected to outpace available memory supply.

11.title: NVTS — Art of Speculation
11.body:
Gallium nitride chips can improve AI-server power conversion through faster switching and lower energy losses.

Navitas, Power Integrations and Infineon are investment candidates, with growth dependent on customer adoption.

12.title: VRT — Art of Speculation
12.body: The Vertiv position consists of April 24 $295 puts targeting a post-earnings retreat to $295, then $278. A 13-session Nasdaq advance and weakness in Chinese liquid-cooling shares support the trade. Weekly max pain is near $290, but implied volatility of 99%-105% leaves the options exposed to a post-earnings volatility collapse.

13.title: MRVL — Art of Speculation
13.body:
Marvell reported second-quarter revenue of $2.739 billion and third-quarter guidance of $3.15 billion.

Growth and Google-related expectations appear largely priced in. The long-term outlook remains positive, but a better entry before the midterm elections is preferred.

14.title: ARM — Art of Speculation
14.body:
Arm's AI and data-center outlook remains positive, but a forward earnings multiple near 190 times leaves little margin of safety.

A long-term entry would wait for a price correction or stronger earnings evidence.

15.title: MSFT — Bill Ackman
15.body:
At June 30, Microsoft traded at 19 times estimated next-12-month earnings.

Pershing Square was 8% below cost including dividends despite a 1% quarterly gain. Its three-to-five-year estimate combines EPS growth and dividend yield at 19% annually.

Copilot can reach existing Office customers, while Azure supplies AI computing. Adoption must justify the infrastructure spending.

16.title: PSUS — Bill Ackman
16.body: Pershing Square USA, the listed investment fund, has put more of its available capital to work and added holdings, expanding the portfolio that supports its value.

17.title: FNMA / FMCC — Bill Ackman
17.body:
Fannie Mae shares fell 39% and Freddie Mac shares fell 41% in the first half of the year. Pershing Square remains optimistic about privatization and the companies' ability to rebuild capital.

Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac can build capital by keeping their earnings while privatization is stalled. Pershing Square remains invested, with further upside dependent on a favorable government decision.

18.title: HHH — Bill Ackman
18.body:
Howard Hughes is expanding from property into insurance through Vantage, with Pershing Square managing investments. Longer-term bonds were largely replaced with short US Treasuries and stocks.

The goal is at least 20% return on equity. Most of the $2.5-$3bn excess property cash expected over three to five years would fund insurance. Buying Vantage at 1.4x book value, then reinvesting at book value, supports the plan.

19.title: UBER — Bill Ackman
19.body:
At June 30, Uber traded at 19 times estimated next-twelve-month earnings after falling 12% year to date.

Pershing Square projected 25% annual growth over three to five years under its earnings-growth measure that includes dividend yield.

Partnerships let Uber participate in driverless transport while retaining the customer relationship. Working with several vehicle operators can support demand and earnings, provided Uber earns an attractive share of each trip.

20.title: XYZ — Cathie Wood
20.body: Block is developing products faster after Jack Dorsey's reorganization and greater use of AI. Cash App and Square have both completed work and projects still underway.

21.title: SHOP — Cathie Wood
21.body: AI shopping is helping customers discover smaller Shopify merchants, suggesting its benefits can extend beyond the platform's largest sellers.

22.title: CRCL / MA / V — Cathie Wood
22.body: Circle could benefit as new technology changes payments. That disruption may also make Visa and Mastercard's past stock returns harder to repeat.

23.title: BTC — Cathie Wood
23.body:
Bitcoin's open-source security teams need trusted access to leading AI models because attackers already use AI.

The Bitcoin Policy Institute is asking major AI labs to provide that access to qualified defenders.

24.title: CRSP — Cathie Wood
24.body:
CRISPR Therapeutics already generates revenue from treatments for sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia.

Its wider target markets, including cardiovascular disease, could collectively be worth trillions of dollars.

25.title: NVDA — Jerry Capital
25.body: Trying the Instinct AI assistant suggests agents could use far more computing than expected. Nvidia is one way to invest in that demand.

26.title: SHOP — Jerry Capital
26.body:
An agent that chooses stores and products controls an important part of the customer relationship.

Shopify may remain essential to merchants while losing influence over where buyers shop. That shift can give the agent more negotiating power over the platform processing the purchase.

27.title: GPN — Jerry Capital
27.body:
Global Payments looks cheap at $95 if the business stays stable and earnings become cash.

Wolfe's EPS forecasts of $13.71 for 2026 and $16.26 for 2027 imply 6.9x and 5.8x earnings. Its $110 target offers about 16% upside before dividends. If owners receive only $12-$13 after recurring costs, the multiple is 7-8x. Paying $70 requires avoiding decline; $95 needs stability, $110 a successful operating plan, and $130-$150 sustained growth and cash flow.

28.title: GOOG — Jerry Capital
28.body: Google's lack of a leading model and a compelling personal agent increases the threat to search. Management changes are called for.

29.title: AMZN — Jerry Capital
29.body:
Institutional lending against GPUs could let independent clouds build before securing customers, at borrowing costs closer to those of the largest providers.

That would weaken one important advantage of the cloud leaders.

30.title: BE — 3X Long Labubu
30.body:
The entire Bloom Energy position was sold after hours on September 4.

The long-term outlook remains positive: fuel cells can supply on-site electricity when permits and grid connections delay data centers.

31.title: AMD / INTC / ARM — 3X Long Labubu
31.body: Intel had been sold to avoid earnings risk, while AMD and Arm remained held. CPU shortages were judged more severe than expected as agent workloads increased demand.

32.title: SNDK — 3X Long Labubu
32.body: SanDisk's contracts can commit customers to keep paying without fixing product prices. That more dependable demand is the investment argument; future margins still depend on pricing.

33.title: TLT / GLD — 3X Long Labubu
33.body: TLT and GLD calls offered a short-term way to benefit if policy action eased pressure from a U.S. ten-year yield near 4.6%. The trade depended on a weekend catalyst.

34.title: ENTG / ONTO — 3X Long Labubu
34.body:
Semiconductor exposure stayed partial until the market confirmed a durable rebound.

The plan kept 20%-25% in TQQQ, Micron and SanDisk, doubled near S&P 500 6,150, and doubled again only after extreme downside or a bullish 20-day/50-day moving-average crossover. Key downside references were S&P 500 6,150 and Nasdaq 100 22,200, with geopolitical risk still active.

35.title: COPX / COPP / ICOP — mon
35.body: Demand from data centers, chips and defense supports a long-term bullish copper view. COPX, COPP and ICOP are the named fund choices, with copper also favored as a safe-haven investment.

36.title: UAMY — mon
36.body: United States Antimony looks attractive after a report that a Chinese-owned Canadian antimony mine closed. It offers another source of this critical mineral, which is separate from rare earths.

37.title: DUOL / AAPL — mon
37.body: Apple's new live-translation feature threatens demand for Duolingo's language-learning service.

38.title: VELO — mon
38.body:
Velo3D has a five-year defense procurement agreement worth up to $9.8 million.

It provides a way for the Defense Logistics Agency to order approved 3D-printed metal replacement parts. Velo3D earns revenue only as individual orders are issued. Becoming an approved supplier could help it win repeat work across the military.

39.title: SATL — mon
39.body:
Satellogic has not yet been moved to the long-term portfolio.

That decision depends on Merlin's success, with a first launch expected in October 2026 and full operating capability in the first half of 2027.

40.title: TTWO — Q-Cap
40.body: If the delay rumor is right, releasing GTA VI first and adding its online mode later could keep players spending after the initial excitement fades.

41.title: ADBE / META — Q-Cap
41.body: Adobe's situation differs from Meta's earlier slump. Meta could cut spending on an expensive side project while retaining a strong advertising business; Adobe faces AI competition in its core software. Prior buybacks do not resolve that challenge.

42.title: ORCL / QQQ — Q-Cap
42.body: Oracle has underperformed QQQ by roughly 75% over the previous year. A recovery depends on stable gross margins, confirmation of its large backlog and no further construction delays.

43.title: KO — Q-Cap
43.body: Coca-Cola looked expensive at more than twice Ferrari's price-to-free-cash-flow multiple, despite similar EBITDA margins and roughly half the expected growth.

44.title: SNOW — Q-Cap
44.body: Access to enterprise data could matter more than the AI model itself. Repeated discussions with software-industry contacts placed Snowflake in a central gatekeeping role.

45.title: SNDK / MU / 000660.KS / 285A.T / DRAM — Ren
45.body:
Memory looks like a multi-year shortage rather than a normal cycle.

Goldman expects DRAM, NAND and HBM supply to remain tight into 2028 as AI-server demand grows, capacity expands slowly and HBM consumes wafers that would otherwise serve conventional DRAM. Preferred exposure includes SK hynix, Kioxia, SanDisk and Micron.

46.title: LITE — Ren
46.body: Lumentum reported $1.01 billion revenue, up 109% year over year, and guided next-quarter revenue near $1.25 billion at roughly 40% operating margin. Demand for optical interconnects remains strong.

47.title: CODA — Ren
47.body:
Coda Octopus's Echoscope sonar can work in zero-visibility water, offering a potential role in clearing mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

Existing special-operations and explosive-ordnance contracts, reported 30% annual revenue growth and no debt support the bullish view.

48.title: MU — Ren
48.body: Micron's weak share-price reaction suggests the earnings beat was already priced in. Growth alone was insufficient to exceed market expectations.

49.title: LITE / AAOI / COHR / MRVL / CRDO / GLW / SIVE.ST — Ren
49.body:
Goldman's September 7 model raised the photonics outlook while moving co-packaged optics growth later.

It forecast optical modules at $68 billion in 2026, $131 billion in 2027 and $148 billion in 2028. 800G-and-faster volume was 78 million units in 2026 and was expected to rise 84% in 2027. Goldman cut 2026 CPO estimates by 33% but raised 2028 by 105%.

The basket included Lumentum, Coherent, Marvell, Corning, AAOI, AXT and Sivers; Credo remained a cautious long-term holding.

LITE / AAOI / COHR / SIVE.ST / MRVL source image

50.title: CRWD — Traderstewie
50.body: Closed the CrowdStrike trade at a loss on July 28 after the shares fell below their 50-day moving average. The failed reversal removed the support for staying in the trade.

51.title: AMD — Traderstewie
51.body: AMD's pullback is occurring on lighter volume. Holding above the previous low would show buyers stepping in sooner and strengthen the case for another advance.

52.title: CSCO — Traderstewie
52.body: Cisco is holding near its 20-day exponential moving average after a sharp May rally. Renewed buying from that support could extend the advance.

53.title: HIMX — Traderstewie
53.body: Himax's opening strength reversed during the session. The failed gap made it unattractive for the proposed near-term trade.

54.title: AAOI — Traderstewie
54.body: Applied Optoelectronics continued to show relative strength, with its rising 20-day exponential moving average supporting repeated tests.

55.title: BN — Bill Ackman
55.body:
At June 30, Brookfield traded at 14 times estimated next-12-month earnings.

Dividend-inclusive returns were 5% for the quarter and -7% year to date. Pershing Square's three-to-five-year estimate combines EPS growth and dividend yield at 20% annually.

Limited assessed private-credit and software risks support the valuation case. Earnings and investment profits offer upside, but asset-sale timing makes quarterly results uneven.

56.title: META — Bill Ackman
56.body:
At June 30, Meta traded at 18 times estimated next-12-month earnings, down 1% for the quarter and 15% year to date.

Pershing Square projected 22% annual growth over three to five years, combining EPS growth and dividend yield.

AI recommendations and ad targeting could improve engagement and advertisers' results. Renting unused computing could add sales. These benefits must outweigh infrastructure costs.

57.title: QSR — Bill Ackman
57.body:
At June 30, Restaurant Brands traded at 17 times estimated next-12-month earnings.

Dividend-inclusive returns were -1% for the quarter and 8% year to date. Pershing Square's three-to-five-year estimate combines EPS growth and dividend yield at 15% annually.

Lasting improvements at Burger King and overseas restaurants, limited capital needs and buybacks could raise earnings per share.

58.title: AMZN — Bill Ackman
58.body:
At June 30, Amazon traded at 27 times estimated next-12-month earnings.

Dividend-inclusive returns were 14% for the quarter and 3% year to date. Pershing Square's three-to-five-year estimate combines EPS growth and dividend yield at 24% annually.

AI demand supports AWS, while e-commerce growth and better operations can lift retail margins. Data-center spending must earn adequate returns.

59.title: V / MA — Bill Ackman
59.body:
Visa and Mastercard looked attractive near 22x forward earnings after AI, stablecoin and regulatory fears.

Stated multiples later reached 23x and 24x; expected three-to-five-year EPS growth plus dividend yield was 16% and 18% annually.

Broad merchant acceptance and fraud protection support their role as payments change. US rate-cap and routing proposals had stalled; estimated damage from routing legislation was limited even if passed.

source.label: Pershing Square August 12, 2026 joint letter - page 18

60.title: NFLX — Bill Ackman
60.body:
The new Netflix holding is separate from the 2022 investment.

At June 30 it was 11% below cost and traded at 21x forward earnings. Pershing Square's three-to-five-year estimate combines EPS growth and dividend yield at 19% annually.

A stronger global audience spreads content costs across more users, allowing profit to outgrow sales. Ads and buybacks add potential, while AI-generated video poses competition.

61.title: SPGI — Bill Ackman
61.body:
Pershing Square returned to S&P Global after owning it in 2017.

At June 30, it was 3% below cost at 19x forward earnings. The three-to-five-year estimate for earnings growth plus dividends was 15% annually.

Ratings, indices and proprietary data can offset AI pressure on desktop software. High-single-digit sales growth may persist even if Market Intelligence misses 6%-8%. Roughly 4% annual share-count reduction helps earnings; mid-20s stock returns also need a higher valuation.

source.label: Pershing Square August 12, 2026 joint letter - page 21

62.title: ICE — Bill Ackman
62.body:
Intercontinental Exchange was bought after June 30 at about 17x forward earnings. Pershing Square's three-to-five-year estimate for earnings growth plus dividends was 15% annually.

Linked exchanges and clearing services protect its energy business. Volatility, hedging, data and buybacks support earnings; a mortgage recovery adds upside. A mid-20s annualized stock return also needs the valuation to recover toward year-earlier levels.

source.label: Pershing Square August 12, 2026 joint letter - page 23

63.title: ALC — Bill Ackman
63.body:
Alcon's surgical equipment generates recurring consumables sales, supporting a new investment at about 18 times forward earnings after June 30.

Its installed base of 30,000 units, expected sales growth of 6%-8% and a potential margin increase from roughly 20% to at least 25% could drive mid-teens earnings growth.

A $1.5 billion buyback authorization adds support. AURN001, an experimental eye therapy in Phase 3 development, offers further upside if the FDA approves it.

source.label: Pershing Square August 12, 2026 joint letter - page 23

64.title: UMG.AS — Bill Ackman
64.body:
AI-generated uploads are growing rapidly without a matching increase in listening.

Spotify's stream counts also differ from royalty revenue because plays in some markets earn less. Universal Music's major artists, artist-centered payments, price increases and Virgin Music services could help sustain its position.

65.title: PSH.L — Bill Ackman
65.body:
Pershing Square Holdings lets investors buy businesses its managers consider cheap at an additional discount to the value of the fund's assets.

That discount is near a record. More outreach to investors and financial advisers could help narrow it.

source.label: PSH 2026 interim report, joint manager letter, printed page 8

66.title: TSLA — Cathie Wood
66.body:
A smooth driverless Tesla Robotaxi ride in Austin shows more than ten years of real-world AI training reaching a working service.

A reported $75 parking ticket also raises an operating-cost question, prompting ARK to add traffic and parking violations to its Tesla model.

67.title: ATAI — Cathie Wood
67.body:
ATAI's clinical trials support the potential of psychedelic treatments for treatment-resistant depression.

PTSD and other mental-health conditions may offer further applications as the research develops.

68.title: UBER — Cathie Wood
68.body:
Autonomous vehicles could take Uber's busiest, most profitable trips first.

Lower driver earnings could then push drivers away and force Uber to raise prices while autonomous rivals charge less. That deterioration could start slowly and then accelerate.

69.title: HOOD — Cathie Wood
69.body: Attracting more users would improve Robinhood's crypto liquidity and credibility. Whether on-chain activity brings new Robinhood customers remains the key question.

70.title: AVGO — Cathie Wood
70.body: Broadcom's role in OpenAI's Jalapeno inference chip supports a positive view of its custom AI hardware business. Power efficiency and fast response times matter as AI usage grows.

71.title: ARKY — Cathie Wood
71.body: ARKY uses options and other derivatives to create equity-linked notes tied to innovation stocks. It targets a 17.5% coupon, with returns still exposed to the risks of the underlying structure.

72.title: HOOD — Art of Speculation
72.body:
With Robinhood approaching $150, the medium-to-long-term target is $300.

Growth could come from tokenized assets, prediction-market exchange and clearing services, AI-assisted accounts and prospective children's accounts. The May purchase is now considered too small, and no further additions have been made.

73.title: SNDK — Art of Speculation
73.body:
SanDisk's implied earnings move of about 15% may understate a potential move above 20%.

Buying calls and puts could let one profitable leg outweigh the other, but a smaller-than-priced move could lose money on both. The earlier Intel profit calculation is a hypothetical example.

74.title: GOLD — Art of Speculation
74.body:
Currency debasement, geopolitical fragmentation and the absence of counterparty risk support a long-term gold allocation.

Preferred entries are $4,000 and $3,500, though the 200-day average near $4,300 could hold first. Gold is the least certain of the four opportunities under consideration.

75.title: QQQ — Art of Speculation
75.body: A confirmed retest of QQQ's prior $636 high would offer a long-term addition opportunity. The breakout needs to hold and the price resume higher.

76.title: HIMS — Art of Speculation
76.body: Hims & Hers is preferred to Oklo for an earnings trade because short positioning is higher, at about 33% versus 18%.

77.title: SPY / QQQ — Art of Speculation
77.body:
SPY support at $756-$760 needs a convincing reversal to keep a return toward the highs plausible. A decisive break below $756 points toward $725-$730, while the weekly uptrend could survive.

QQQ support at $700-$702 combines a prior gap and its 20-week average within a $700-$730 range. Neither has a clear daily bottom signal yet.

78.title: PLTR — Art of Speculation
78.body:
Palantir's enterprise AI platform and commercial growth support its valuation despite weak software sentiment.

A 125-times forward earnings multiple looks reasonable only if U.S. commercial growth stays above 100%. Support at $136 matters, and a confirmed break above the descending trendline is still needed.

79.title: RDDT — Art of Speculation
79.body: Reddit's long-term trendline near $130 is the preferred support area. Its human conversation data is valuable for AI training.

80.title: MSFT — Art of Speculation
80.body: Microsoft has fallen below its $430 breakout and failed to hold the 200-day moving average. A prompt recovery would be needed to make the breakdown temporary.

81.title: META — Art of Speculation
81.body: Meta's support sits at $580-$585, with a lower gap at $574. Possible new issuance adds financing concerns.

82.title: AMZN — Art of Speculation
82.body: AWS growth and Amazon's operating performance remain strong, but large capital requirements and a long payback period limit the case for a higher valuation.

83.title: GOOGL — Art of Speculation
83.body: Alphabet's stronger earnings reaction reflects AI-supported growth alongside spending that investors appear more willing to accept. The balance between investment and returns supports the shares.

84.title: COIN — Art of Speculation
84.body: Coinbase remains a holding. Regulatory clarity could attract institutional activity, though restrictions on passive stablecoin rewards may require product changes. A prospective compromise would permit usage-based rewards, with the legislative outcome still pending.

85.title: CORZ — Art of Speculation
85.body:
Core Scientific looks like the lower-risk AI hosting company because customers help fund construction and pay even when they do not use the capacity.

Its dependence on CoreWeave remains the main risk. New generations of chips will still need buildings and power.

86.title: APLD — Art of Speculation
86.body: Applied Digital looks expensive at 27 times sales, the highest valuation among the compared hosting companies. Construction delays or disappointing results could therefore be costly for shareholders.

87.title: FLNC / EOSE — Art of Speculation
87.body:
Fluence and Eos Energy were both positioned as underappreciated storage names.

Fluence's roughly 31% short interest could amplify a near-term squeeze, while the broader thesis is that capital may rotate from crowded memory and optics into data centers and storage.

88.title: EOSE — Art of Speculation
88.body:
Eos Energy's cup-and-handle setup targets around $11, with roughly 33% short interest and three to four days to cover.

Strong data-center storage demand could support an earnings surprise, though the pre-earnings rally raises expectations.

89.title: ONDS — Art of Speculation
89.body: Favorable May 14 results support a possible Ondas move to $22-$23 by August or September.

90.title: BABA — Art of Speculation
90.body:
Alibaba's earnings and the China visit offer separate near-term catalysts.

Entry is preferred before May 13, with reassessment after May 15 because geopolitical statements could erase the expected benefit.

91.title: CHRN — Art of Speculation
91.body: ChronoScale's prospective cloud transition, small public float and Applied Digital ownership could amplify price moves. Severe illiquidity also magnifies downside, favoring an allocation of about 1%.

92.title: NNE / OKLO — Art of Speculation
92.body:
Nano Nuclear is preferred to the more crowded Oklo because of its smaller valuation and proposed industry partnerships.

Its Supermicro arrangement is a memorandum of understanding, while meaningful revenue is not expected until 2029.

93.title: NRGV — Art of Speculation
93.body:
Energy Vault's proposed expansion into storage integration, asset operation and modular AI facilities looks underappreciated.

Delivery is essential, and the speculative risk favors a position of about 1%.

94.title: CEG — Art of Speculation
94.body:
Constellation Energy should be deferred until its technical setup improves.

Reported share issuance and another trendline break favor waiting for daily RSI to become oversold or for support at a lower trendline, potentially around late June.

95.title: BWXT — Art of Speculation
95.body: BWX Technologies makes and services nuclear equipment for naval and commercial customers. It can benefit across reactor types without needing one new design to win.

96.title: CCJ / UEC — Art of Speculation
96.body: Cameco is favored as an established uranium producer with operating history and cash generation. Uranium Energy offers a more aggressive alternative focused on U.S. production.

97.title: OKLO — Art of Speculation
97.body:
Oklo's planned reactor deployments and customer pipeline could provide upside if projects enter operation.

Its large valuation, lack of current revenue and absence of operating reactors make the investment speculative.

98.title: UEC — Art of Speculation
98.body: Uranium Energy could gain business as the US expands nuclear-fuel production and replaces imports. Its small size also brings substantial downside risk.

99.title: BA — Art of Speculation
99.body: Boeing is the preferred trade ahead of the China visit because an aircraft agreement could bring orders and a brief rally. Delivery problems and selling after the announcement favor an exit by May 15.

100.title: LNG — Art of Speculation
100.body: Cheniere is the preferred trade if China agrees to buy more liquefied natural gas under a long-term contract. The proposed entry is before May 13 for a possible news-driven rally.

101.title: BIDU — Art of Speculation
101.body: Baidu's proposed Kunlunxin listing could unlock value independently of the China visit.

102.title: NVDA / QCOM — Art of Speculation
102.body:
A dip before the China visit could offer a short-term entry in Nvidia and Qualcomm.

The advice is to exit by May 15 because national-security limits may constrain the news and investors could sell after announcements.

103.title: DOCN — Art of Speculation
103.body:
DigitalOcean offers smaller AI companies simple, flexible inference infrastructure.

Growing AI customer adoption suggests an expansion beyond inexpensive general hosting, with continued paid use essential to revenue growth.

104.title: TEAM — Art of Speculation
104.body:
Jira and Confluence hold enterprise data and context that AI agents need.

Rovo adoption and customer commitments were cited as evidence that AI could strengthen reliance on Atlassian's workflow platform.

105.title: SNOW — Art of Speculation
105.body:
Product revenue, retention and backlog growth support Snowflake's paid AI-workload opportunity.

A small position was opened the prior week. The $6 billion AWS arrangement commits Snowflake to spending over five years; it is not revenue to Snowflake.

106.title: CRM — Art of Speculation
106.body:
Salesforce has a large business customer base, but Agentforce has not yet clearly accelerated recurring revenue.

Moving away from per-employee pricing also creates uncertainty. The shares could recover with software stocks before those business questions are settled.

107.title: BAND / CRM — Art of Speculation
107.body:
Bandwidth's owned communications network suits low-latency AI voice agents.

Its Salesforce relationship supports the commercial opportunity, with paid adoption and actual call traffic essential to growth.

108.title: TWLO — Art of Speculation
108.body: Twilio can earn more when AI agents make calls and send messages. Voice revenue is already up 20% year over year, suggesting that demand is producing sales.

109.title: ZM — Art of Speculation
109.body: Zoom offers a higher-risk turnaround if AI Companion and virtual agents expand its role in phone, customer-service and collaboration workflows. A higher valuation depends on that adoption.

110.title: DDOG — Art of Speculation
110.body: Datadog monitors AI-agent errors, behavior and operating costs. Wider enterprise deployment could increase demand for those services, creating a longer-term opportunity that requires patience.

111.title: TSEM — Art of Speculation
111.body:
Tower Semiconductor's foundry serves multiple silicon-photonics architectures.

Signed 2027 contracts of $1.3 billion and $290 million in capacity prepayments support expansion. Larger 2028 contracts remain under negotiation.

112.title: SIVE.ST — Art of Speculation
112.body:
Putting optical links next to AI chips could create a shortage of the lasers Sivers supplies.

Suggested relationships with large cloud companies remain supply-chain inferences, not confirmed customers.

113.title: AAOI — Art of Speculation
113.body: Applied Optoelectronics remains a small position because its earnings and production plans can bring large share-price swings.

114.title: AXTI — Art of Speculation
114.body: AXT makes indium-phosphide materials used in lasers. More laser demand could bring sales, but Chinese export permits can delay shipments, favoring a small position.

115.title: CIEN — Art of Speculation
115.body: Ciena's operating growth supports the business case, but its valuation and reported insider selling favor waiting for a pullback.

116.title: FPS — Art of Speculation
116.body:
Forgent Power Solutions supplies customized power-distribution equipment for data centers and the grid.

Rising orders and short delivery times support growth. The proposed entry is a small breakout purchase or a pullback toward $44 and the 20-day moving average near $40.

117.title: IGV — Art of Speculation
117.body: IGV could remain in a $90-$107 range for several months before an eventual breakout. A temporary trendline break need not invalidate the longer-term recovery.

118.title: SOFI — Art of Speculation
118.body: SoFi's 200-week moving average near $15.50 is the first level to watch, while $13 is preferred for a deeper long-term entry. Improving rate expectations and risk appetite support the opportunity.

119.title: APP — Art of Speculation
119.body: AppLovin looks strong after regaining its 200-day moving average. A confirmed double-bottom breakout above $520 would target $690.

120.title: INTU — Art of Speculation
120.body: Intuit fell 20% despite results exceeding expectations. AI tools threaten the future value of traditional tax preparation and accounting software.

121.title: FCX — Art of Speculation
121.body: Freeport-McMoRan could pull back if copper and silver weaken as expected.

122.title: CRWD — Art of Speculation
122.body: AI expands the data and systems requiring protection, supporting demand for CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks. Cybersecurity looks attractive as capital rotates away from crowded hardware shares.

123.title: CRDO — Art of Speculation
123.body:
Credo's low-power interconnects serve rising demand for high-speed AI-server connections.

MicroLED could strengthen its position if commercial adoption improves energy efficiency and density. Astera Labs was selected instead when the two investments were previously compared.

124.title: RKLB — Art of Speculation
124.body: Rocket Lab could lose some scarcity premium once investors can buy SpaceX directly. A double top around $140-$150 could offer a short opportunity after pre-listing enthusiasm.

125.title: TLT — Art of Speculation
125.body: Heavy Treasury issuance, reduced foreign demand and energy-driven inflation could keep long-term yields elevated, making the TLT long-duration Treasury ETF unattractive.

126.title: ANET — Art of Speculation
126.body:
Arista Networks is favored for large-scale Ethernet cluster networking, a different role from in-rack NVLink.

Early deployments and optical-component costs could pressure margins, while improvements in open Ethernet performance support the longer-term opportunity.

127.title: BB — Art of Speculation
127.body: January 2028 BlackBerry long-dated options were purchased after the shares broke above a trendline near $7.40. Near-term resistance at $12-$14 argues against chasing the rally.

128.title: ERIC — Art of Speculation
128.body: Ericsson's established radio-access-network business could participate in AI-enabled mobile networks. Commercial models and carrier spending schedules remain uncertain.

129.title: ADI — Art of Speculation
129.body:
Analog Devices supplies radio-frequency components, data converters, power management and signal-processing chips for wireless and industrial systems.

More complex edge AI and wireless networks could increase demand as deployment expands.

130.title: NET / NOK / MRVL / QCOM — Art of Speculation
130.body: Cloudflare's software supports AI inference and distributed computing near users. It is worth watching alongside the complementary physical networks and chips supplied by Nokia, Marvell and Qualcomm.

131.title: SYM — Art of Speculation
131.body: Symbotic is a preferred robotics deployment company. Warehouse automation and Walmart orders support its revenue opportunity as enterprise supply chains adopt automation.

132.title: 6830.TW — Art of Speculation
132.body:
MSSCorps could benefit as early optical-loss detection helps avoid scrapping expensive AI chip packages.

The investment depends on equipment shipments, monthly revenue exceeding the estimated NT$220 million break-even level and the outcome of an unresolved patent dispute. Potential customer leads still need to become contracts.

133.title: IWM — Art of Speculation
133.body: A confirmed large breakout could take IWM toward $300 over the coming months. Broader small-cap participation would signal improving risk appetite, with options activity around $290-$300 supporting the setup.

134.title: LRCX / ASML — Art of Speculation
134.body: Higher memory profits could encourage chipmakers to expand factories, creating demand for Lam Research and ASML equipment. The opportunity depends on those spending plans becoming equipment orders.

135.title: MDB / SNOW — Art of Speculation
135.body:
MongoDB and Snowflake show investors repricing data-layer software as AI agents increase demand for real-time data, vector search, governance and cloud infrastructure.

MongoDB's revenue grew 25%, while remaining performance obligations grew faster. Sharp after-hours swings show continued valuation disagreement.

136.title: DELL — Art of Speculation
136.body:
Dell reported $16.1 billion of quarterly AI-server revenue and raised full-year AI-server revenue guidance to $60 billion.

The results support strong AI-infrastructure demand, with the forecast dependent on continued delivery.

137.title: AMKR — Art of Speculation
137.body: Amkor's packaging role and developing bull flag support a conditional $100 target. More consolidation is expected before a breakout.

138.title: SMR — Art of Speculation
138.body: NuScale appears close to a breakout. Its small size calls for careful position sizing and risk control.

139.title: ADBE — Art of Speculation
139.body: Adobe could rebound toward $300 and then $330 if it breaks its descending trendline. Oversold positioning and potential short covering after a modest earnings surprise support the speculative trade.

140.title: TTMI — Art of Speculation
140.body: TTM Technologies makes circuit boards for AI infrastructure. The preferred entry is a pullback to its 20-day average.

141.title: RDW — Art of Speculation
141.body: The plan is to buy Redwire near $17.50 after the sector pullback and hold until the expected SpaceX listing day. Continued pre-listing space-sector enthusiasm supports the trade.

142.title: DXYZ — Art of Speculation
142.body: Destiny Tech100 remains bearish after a double top and failed neckline retest. Rebounds are favored for exits.

143.title: AAPL — Art of Speculation
143.body:
Apple's initial AI launch excludes the EU and China, limiting how many customers it can reach.

At 36.5 times earnings versus a five-year average of 27.6 times, the price needs adoption and revenue to justify it.

144.title: SNOW / DDOG / MDB / CRWD / PANW / INOD / NOW / WDAY / ADBE / INTU / CRM / TEAM — 3X Long Labubu
144.body:
Snowflake, Datadog, MongoDB, CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks and Innodata show signs of genuine buying.

ServiceNow, Workday, Adobe, Intuit, Salesforce and Atlassian look less convincing. The next sessions will test whether demand persists beyond short covering in hardware-software pair trades.

145.title: NBIS / MSFT — 3X Long Labubu
145.body:
Rising long-term interest rates make expansion harder for AI-chip rental companies that rely on loans, new shares and customer deposits.

Microsoft can fund more of its construction from existing business cash flow. Nebius may also improve its position if earnings show a strong rise in operating profit.

146.title: NBIS / IREN / CRWV — 3X Long Labubu
146.body:
Nebius, IREN and CoreWeave all have AI-infrastructure upside, but their strengths differ.

Nebius has the strongest technology and potential software margins. IREN has the strongest execution but greater financing risk. CoreWeave has strong access to capital but more debt exposure.

147.title: QCOM — 3X Long Labubu
147.body: Qualcomm looked positioned for further upside as successive ByteDance-related reports drove repeated rallies. Leveraged exposure increased after the shares reached $214.50.

148.title: DXYZ / VOYG — 3X Long Labubu
148.body:
Investing directly in Anthropic at a $900 billion valuation looks less attractive than DXYZ after setup and legal costs, management fees, carried interest and a six-month post-IPO lockup.

A difficult prior VOYG lockup reinforces the preference for liquidity.

149.title: CIEN / NOK / GOOG / AMZN — 3X Long Labubu
149.body:
Indium phosphide and inter-data-center networking are Nokia's main attractions; AI-RAN looks overhyped.

Nokia reportedly secured a Google networking contract because Ciena lacked capacity. More cloud-provider orders, potentially from Amazon, are expected.

150.title: LITE — 3X Long Labubu
150.body: Strong demand could support even less differentiated component suppliers, making them attractive despite concerns about commodity chips.

151.title: SANM / AMD / FLEX — 3X Long Labubu
151.body: Sanmina was bought after hours. Its own results, strong Flex results and AMD earnings support the purchase. Its AMD system-manufacturing relationship through ZT Systems is the most important driver.

152.title: RMBS — 3X Long Labubu
152.body: Rambus was expected to benefit from large CPU demand and deliveries. It was not expected to capture the CPU price increase caused by the shortage itself; that benefit was attributed to CPU companies.

153.title: SMTC — 3X Long Labubu
153.body: Semtech's product breadth across copper and optical communications supports a favorable view of its fundamentals and renewed research. The last trade in the company was two years earlier.

154.title: ASTS — 3X Long Labubu
154.body: Repairable Blue Origin infrastructure and a targeted return to flight before year-end support AST SpaceMobile's launch outlook. The schedule remains a target, not a completed repair.

155.title: SNOW — 3X Long Labubu
155.body: Snowflake reclaimed the $220-$230 area after hours. The trade depends on holding $230.

156.title: GLD — 3X Long Labubu
156.body:
Gold was favored before the Federal Reserve meeting because the rate path and institutional credibility remained uncertain.

A September rate increase was the key bearish scenario. The inflation forecast was core CPI of 0.2% month over month and 2.5% year over year; a weak employment report was also expected.

157.title: BTC / ETH — 3X Long Labubu
157.body: Ahead of CPI, Bitcoin and gold futures were described as being at the lower edge of bullish flags. The market reaction remained uncertain even though core CPI was expected at 0.2%.

158.title: IWM — 3X Long Labubu
158.body:
Russell futures are at key support, while S&P 500 futures have broken below their 50-day exponential moving average and need to reclaim 7,620-7,630.

The market reaction remains uncertain despite an expected 0.2% core CPI print.

159.title: SMCI — 3X Long Labubu
159.body: Super Micro remains unattractive because of alleged H-series export misconduct. Potential consequences include forced delisting, investor lawsuits, executive imprisonment and regulatory fines.

160.title: AMZN — 3X Long Labubu
160.body: Amazon's infrastructure investment may pay back faster than the conservative period of under three years, although more slowly than DeepSeek's claimed ten months.

161.title: AMZN — 3X Long Labubu
161.body: The next Amazon training chip was described as repeatedly delayed. A release and large-scale deployment in Q4 was the condition for a favorable reassessment comparable to Google's.

162.title: AAOI — 3X Long Labubu
162.body: Applied Optoelectronics' earnings call was better than expected, with management committing to avoid overpromising against demand.

163.title: ARM — 3X Long Labubu
163.body: Arm's limited reaction to investigation headlines and relative strength during a broad semiconductor decline created a strong buy signal.

164.title: TE / F / FCEL / FLNC / FSLR — 3X Long Labubu
164.body:
T1 Energy, FuelCell Energy, Fluence, Ford, Nextracker and First Solar were actively swing-traded over the preceding two weeks.

Strong charts and unusual call flows may reflect a shift toward alternative energy, but the trades remain short term.

165.title: APP — 3X Long Labubu
165.body: Selling AppLovin puts looks unattractive because the stock is highly sensitive to macroeconomic conditions.

166.title: ASTS — 3X Long Labubu
166.body: Redwire lacks momentum. The discussed Amazon-Globalstar acquisition could pressure AST SpaceMobile.

167.title: GLW — 3X Long Labubu
167.body: Corning earnings look unexciting compared with Chinese peers. Conservative guidance leaves room for a positive catalyst at the following Wednesday's investor day.

168.title: WOLF — 3X Long Labubu
168.body: Institutional risk or compliance limits may discourage Wolfspeed ownership and contribute to its volatility.

169.title: ITB — 3X Long Labubu
169.body: ITB and Rocket could benefit if credible inflation control stabilizes or lowers long-term yields.

170.title: SMH — 3X Long Labubu
170.body:
Falling KOSPI and SMH volatility alongside rising indices suggests a healthier investor mix after leveraged traders were shaken out.

A steady August advance looks more likely than another April-May-style surge.
