171.title: SPCX — 3X Long Labubu
171.body: Investors, employees and insiders reportedly cannot short SpaceX during the lockup. The selloff more likely reflects expected share supply after the lockup expires.

172.title: SATS / SPCX — 3X Long Labubu
172.body: EchoStar's valuation gap may narrow once SpaceX's price stabilizes and investors stop chasing its shares directly.

173.title: TSEM — 3X Long Labubu
173.body: Tower Semiconductor's weekly relative strength reached an all-time high before its share price did, making it a preferred dip-buying candidate.

174.title: AAPL — 3X Long Labubu
174.body: The Apple position helps balance the portfolio's volatility and risk from AI spending.

175.title: MXL — 3X Long Labubu
175.body: MaxLinear was bought after breaking $100 and added at $112. Earlier trades had been sold at $100 resistance; the breakout improves the technical setup.

176.title: VSH — 3X Long Labubu
176.body: Vishay near $52 fits a pullback entry with bullish moving averages and support near the 50-day or eight-week exponential moving average. Strong names should also defend shorter moving averages.

177.title: TSM — 3X Long Labubu
177.body: TSMC earnings were strong, but gross margin missed buy-side expectations. Restraint on price increases appears aimed at protecting the ecosystem, while extreme memory margins look unsustainable.

178.title: RKLB / NASA — 3X Long Labubu
178.body: The broader space-sector short-covering opportunity may be easier to express through the NASA ETF than through a single stock such as Rocket Lab.

179.title: LITE — 3X Long Labubu
179.body: Lumentum and Coherent formed large bearish engulfing candles ahead of earnings. Whether this reflects hedging or informed selling remains unclear.

180.title: MRNA — 3X Long Labubu
180.body: The Moderna trade depends on enthusiasm for AI and the melanoma market. It does not depend on a newly proven AI treatment.

181.title: ARM / INTC — 3X Long Labubu
181.body: Inverse head-and-shoulders patterns in Arm and Intel supported small initial positions with tight stops.

182.title: BTC — 3X Long Labubu
182.body: Bitcoin's high-volume breakout creates a potential entry if it retests $67,000 over the following days.

183.title: WDC / STX — 3X Long Labubu
183.body: Western Digital and Seagate are preferred within storage for higher margins, limited competition and fewer capacity-expansion concerns. A broader memory selloff could still weigh on both.

184.title: CF — Manchurius Hao
184.body: CF Industries faces potential policy intervention, including a Justice Department antitrust investigation. Oil companies offer a simpler, more controllable way to invest in the energy disruption.

185.title: DAR — Manchurius Hao
185.body: A major U.S. ground campaign in Iran could increase military jet-fuel demand, tightening the shared refinery production pool for diesel and civilian aviation fuel.

186.title: 6981.T — Manchurius Hao
186.body:
MLCC shortages could spread beyond high-end products as Japanese and Korean capacity shifts toward AI.

Reduced flexibility in standard-product supply could lift prices more broadly. Fenghua's reported order suspension prompted the reassessment. Murata and Taiyo Yuden are holdings.

187.title: AEHR — Manchurius Hao
187.body:
Aehr's Sonoma systems support package-level burn-in in hyperscaler accelerator production. The next tests are converting $41 million of orders into revenue, follow-on orders and recurring consumables.

Wafer-level testing still needs to progress from evaluation to production. Flash and high-bandwidth flash testing remain earlier-stage opportunities.

188.title: ARM — Manchurius Hao
188.body:
Arm's breakout above a two-year range could lead to rapid acceleration.

Deep out-of-the-money June calls represent about 10% of the portfolio; a 50% option loss would cost roughly 5% of portfolio value.

189.title: SIVE.ST — Manchurius Hao
189.body: Sivers' U.S.-listing story supports a tactical trade, but a 50% one-day rise would trigger an exit.

190.title: BW / GEV / ENR — Manchurius Hao
190.body:
Babcock & Wilcox can deliver gigawatt-scale boiler-and-steam power in roughly 2.5-3 years, faster than combined-cycle turbine systems from GE Vernova and Siemens Energy.

The solution burns more gas, but delayed power can cost a data-center operator more than the efficiency penalty.

191.title: PS — Manchurius Hao
191.body: PS looks attractive because Bill Ackman's management and its differentiated market behavior can diversify the portfolio.

192.title: VICR / CBRS — Manchurius Hao
192.body:
Cerebras concentrates power demand in a wafer-scale processor, while Vicor places the final conversion stage close beneath it.

That architectural fit creates demand for Vicor's previously niche power technology.

193.title: ALAB — Manchurius Hao
193.body: Persistent AI-agent workflows require more context, cached state and data movement. Addressing memory constraints could use capital more efficiently than simply adding GPUs.

194.title: NET — Manchurius Hao
194.body: AI-agent traffic may raise Cloudflare's network costs and website-owner costs without creating comparable profits. Investments with clearer profit opportunities are preferable.

195.title: TE — Manchurius Hao
195.body:
TE offers speculative exposure to domestic solar manufacturing, storage and policy eligibility as a route to more AI power supply.

Solar would complement other power sources. Orders and financial results still need to validate the investment case.

196.title: KSTR / FXI — Manchurius Hao
196.body: KSTR is an example of a Chinese-equity ETF with the desired emphasis on semiconductors. FXI does not fit that objective.

197.title: STRC — Manchurius Hao
197.body: STRC's income model looks fragile if Bitcoin stops rising or new financing dries up. Without those sources of capital, funding the dividend becomes a concern.

198.title: ETH — Manchurius Hao
198.body: Ether resembles an income-paying asset with little visible growth and a potentially shrinking underlying business.

199.title: SMCI — Manchurius Hao
199.body: Staying out of Super Micro looks preferable. It may need to issue shares to buy components for orders that customers have not firmly committed to.

200.title: IBKR / SIVE.ST — Manchurius Hao
200.body:
Interactive Brokers is moving in the right direction by expanding access to international stocks.

Interest in Sivers and other foreign shares shows the demand: easier access can attract investors who currently struggle to trade Swedish, Korean and other non-US listings.

201.title: NVDA — Manchurius Hao
201.body: Exited Nvidia after it broke below the blue support line on the chart.

202.title: WMT — Manchurius Hao
202.body:
Walmart rebounded with volume from its 200-day simple moving average after a sustained decline.

The setup offers a good chance of continuation and a definable stop area, making it worth watching without requiring a trade.

203.title: CBRS — Manchurius Hao
203.body: Cerebras recovered the entire prior week's decline and moved back above its 10-day average, showing greater strength than a normal market rebound.

204.title: STM — Manchurius Hao
204.body: STMicroelectronics supplies radio-frequency components and custom chips for SpaceX and Starlink. That gives it satellite business alongside cars and industry.

205.title: BESI.AS — Manchurius Hao
205.body: BESI is well positioned in advanced packaging and hybrid bonding, highlighting underappreciated European semiconductor capabilities.

206.title: SWMR — Manchurius Hao
206.body: SWMR remains very high risk. Its financial statements show little evidence of an established revenue or profit stream despite the battlefield narrative.

207.title: FSLR — Manchurius Hao
207.body: First Solar looked like the steadier, more reliable solar investment compared with the controversial, higher-risk T1 Energy.

208.title: ORCL — Manchurius Hao
208.body:
Oracle, IBM and Microsoft were above their 20- and 50-day averages while challenging the 200-day average.

Sustained gains that carried the shorter averages above the 200-day average would strengthen the bullish case. Oracle and IBM's newly cleared 200-day averages could provide support.

209.title: INTC — Manchurius Hao
209.body: Another investor's argument about semiconductor capacity and expansion efficiency supported retaining Intel.

210.title: SHEL — Manchurius Hao
210.body: Shell was worth watching after breaking above a high dating to 2000.

211.title: META / GOOG — Manchurius Hao
211.body: Meta's choice to use computing capacity internally for its own AI models appears to have earned stronger market confidence than Google's emphasis on selling capacity externally.

212.title: AXTI / LITE / COHR — Ren
212.body: Record second-quarter indium-phosphide revenue and supply agreements with Lumentum and Coherent support a bullish AXT view. An estimate attributes 80% of indium-phosphide demand to AI.

213.title: ARM — Ren
213.body:
Arm remains held after a reported 250% gain from the March entry.

Its licensing model lets it earn from custom AI processors without paying to build chip factories, while more AI agents create demand for processors to coordinate their tasks.

214.title: VNP.TO — Ren
214.body:
5N Plus offered photonics-materials exposure through high-purity indium antimonide.

Reported 73% EBITDA growth, 353 days of backlog, expanding margins and government-backed catalysts supported the increasingly positive assessment ahead of May 5 earnings.

215.title: TSEM — Ren
215.body: Tower Semiconductor's cited $1.3 billion of signed 2027 contracts and $290 million in prepayments supported its silicon-photonics foundry expansion, alongside a $920 million capital program.

216.title: AEHR — Ren
216.body:
Aehr looked attractive as a trade at the cited $80 after-hours price, down 46% from its August 17 high.

The burn-in and test business still looked sound, with small-cap fund rotation appearing to explain the decline better than weaker operations.

217.title: 300308.SZ — Ren
217.body: Innolight's proposed Hong Kong listing offered another potential route into the photonics theme, where the outlook remained strongly positive.

218.title: 3105.TWO / SIVE.ST — Ren
218.body:
Win Semiconductors looked underpriced as growth accelerated while factories still had room to expand.

EPS was 30 times the prior-year level, revenue grew 28%, and second-quarter guidance called for 14%-16% sequential growth at 60% utilization. Optical links and satellites led demand; AI data-center revenue was expected to more than double. Photodiodes were entering production, indium-phosphide capacity was expanding, and its foundry role offered broader photonics exposure.

219.title: 2802.T — Ren
219.body:
Ajinomoto looked attractive as a supply-bottleneck investment only if it raised Ajinomoto Build-up Film pricing aggressively.

Established relationships with Japanese supply-chain partners could limit its willingness to do so.

220.title: 3363.TWO — Ren
220.body:
FOCI is the largest Taiwanese holding at a cited $2.7bn valuation. Its patented fiber-array connections could reduce customization and delivery time.

A reported sole-supplier role in TSMC's first two COUPE optical-packaging generations supports the case. Weak finances, no parent-company backing and Chinese competition, particularly TFC, remain risks. FOCI supplies the fiber-array component; Shunsin does downstream assembly.

221.title: CBRS — Ren
221.body: Shorting Cerebras looked like the only attractive direction at the prospective IPO valuation discussed by Serenity: above $35 billion, compared with an earlier $8.1 billion valuation.

222.title: ASML — Ren
222.body: ASML offers exposure to continued semiconductor capital spending and foundry expansion.

223.title: UMC — Ren
223.body: UMC has held support well, so the hoped-for pullback may not come. Newer opportunities are preferred for additional purchases.

224.title: 6706.TW — Ren
224.body: Fittech, Taiwan-listed as 6706, looked best positioned to benefit from the supply chains around Browave and FOCI.

225.title: M7U.DE / LITE / COHR / IQE.L / SOI.PA / AVGO — Ren
225.body:
LayTec's process-metrology demand could grow as IQE, Lumentum, Coherent and Broadcom expanded III-V epitaxy capacity.

Its tools addressed a different production stage from AXT's substrates and Soitec's wafers.

226.title: P4O.DE / LITE — Ren
226.body:
A small speculative Plan Optik position was bought around EUR7-8. Further additions required primary confirmation of its proposed supplier relationship with Silex.

The case combined a possible route through Silex and Lumentum into optical switches with glass-interposer opportunities. Management expected series ramps from 2027, but low wafer content might limit revenue growth without price increases. Thin liquidity, weak results and the unconfirmed commercial link remained material risks.

227.title: ADBE / TYL / VEEV / GWRE / PLTR / CRM / WDAY / NOW / GOOG / MSFT / META / BL / NCNO — Ren
227.body:
AI threatens software protected mainly by coding complexity. Regulatory switching costs, embedded data and useful AI products offer stronger defenses.

Tyler, Veeva and Guidewire have compliance barriers; Palantir has data-model lock-in. Salesforce, Workday, Adobe and ServiceNow look unattractive. BlackLine and nCino show regulated customers alone are insufficient. Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta are preferred established AI platforms.

228.title: POET — Ren
228.body: POET looks unattractive in the near term because a new $400 million offering adds dilution and uncertainty after a roughly 200% run. POET's success could still benefit Sivers.

229.title: MRVL — Ren
229.body: Marvell's decline to $255-$270 looked like another buying opportunity, supported by forthcoming S&P 500 inclusion and AI growth.

230.title: 3103.T — Ren
230.body:
Unitika remains a long after a roughly 50% personal gain. Scarce glass fabrics for advanced AI chip packaging support the case despite a pullback.

Customer qualification barriers, reported Qualcomm interest and limited competing capacity could support demand and pricing. Meaningful Nittobo capacity additions are not expected before the second half of 2027. Full-year guidance is JPY110 billion in sales and JPY9.5 billion in operating profit; May 14 results are the next test.

231.title: INTC — Ren
231.body: Intel was up 100% from the January entry. Reported first-quarter revenue growth of 7%, non-GAAP EPS of $0.29 versus $0.01 consensus, and the Nvidia foundry relationship supported continued conviction.

232.title: NVTS / STM / AOSL / FLEX / POWI / ON / IFNNY / VRT / TXN / MPWR / GEV / ADI / ABB / ETN — Ren
232.body:
AI racks moving to 800V DC create demand for power chips, rack systems and grid equipment. Navitas is held.

Chip candidates include STMicroelectronics, Alpha and Omega, Power Integrations, onsemi and Infineon. Flex and Vertiv supply rack systems; GE Vernova, ABB, Eaton, Schneider and Siemens serve buildings and grids. Texas Instruments, Monolithic Power and Analog Devices add analog and power-management exposure.

233.title: NVTS — Ren
233.body:
Navitas remained the chosen long for Nvidia-related 800V high-voltage DC, gallium nitride and silicon carbide demand.

AI-infrastructure revenue reportedly grew 50% sequentially, but a cited valuation of 124 times sales made it the highest-risk, highest-upside choice in the comparison.

234.title: TRT — Ren
234.body:
Trio-Tech remained a long as new AI GPU and CPU burn-in-board orders supported multiyear growth.

Another $2.6 million order brought the cited total above $5 million for the quarter and $10 million for the fiscal year, including March's $5.3 million award.

Revenue grew 124% year over year and semiconductor back-end revenue 141%. A 104,000-square-foot Penang lease supported expansion, while gross-margin pressure remained a risk.

235.title: 6451.TW — Ren
235.body: Shunsin remained a long as its shares approached a 10% limit-up move for a third day. Wiwynn's optical supply-chain display supported continued optimism.

236.title: IQE.L / TSEM / LITE — Ren
236.body:
IQE remains a long after its multi-year indium-phosphide epiwafer agreement with Tower Semiconductor.

A non-Chinese source has strategic value as Tower moves from 200 Gbps pluggables toward 400 Gbps-per-lane modulators and optical circuit switches.

Tower's royalty-free porous-silicon patent license follows the companies' 2022 IP dispute. Existing Lumentum and MACOM relationships also support the supply-chain case. The position was built after declines to 45 and 32.

237.title: MXL — Ren
237.body:
MaxLinear has shipped millions of Keystone chips that process signals in optical connections.

It is expanding from connections between racks into links within larger AI systems. The cited market mix is about 30% within-system connections and 70% between-system connections. Its Annapurna platform adds electrical connections and signal-conditioning chips for the newer designs, broadening the opportunity beyond its existing products.

238.title: AMZN — Ren
238.body:
Mirae Asset Securities research shared by Jukan supports an Amazon rerating after its Anthropic agreement.

Cloud fees, Trainium and Graviton usage, and infrastructure utilization should benefit whichever AI lab wins. CY2026 EV/EBITDA is near a ten-year low.

239.title: ALMU — Ren
239.body: Sivers' established technology and supply chain leave a scaling challenge. Aeluma faces more binary adoption risk, and its additional upside does not appear sufficient to compensate.

240.title: PTON — Ren
240.body: Peloton's strongest growth phase has passed. A return to its former share-price level looks unlikely without another lockdown.

241.title: SOI.PA — Ren
241.body: Soitec's photonics-SOI wafers are important to optical engines. A significant share-price decline would offer a buying opportunity.

242.title: TSM / GOOG — Ren
242.body:
TSMC is a key manufacturing constraint for advanced AI chips, with advanced-node demand around three times supply.

CoWoS capacity is expected to rise from 80,000 to 130,000 wafers monthly by year-end 2026, while MediaTek seeks a sevenfold capacity increase for Google TPU work.

243.title: GOOGL / GOOG — Ren
243.body: Google is the preferred hyperscaler for parking capital after reporting EPS of $5.11 versus $2.63 expected and revenue of $109.9 billion versus $107.2 billion. Shares rose about 3% after hours.

244.title: 6830.TW — Ren
244.body:
MSSCorps could expand materials and failure analysis into silicon-photonics equipment and licensing, but commercialization is still ahead.

Revenue grew 14.35% annually in 2015-2025 to NT$2.18bn. Its 2026 presentation describes three in-house optical-chip tools and planned production/testing equipment. Optical and AI chips are guided from 7% to 7.7% of sales. New overseas sites raised foreign revenue share from 15%-20% to 30%-35%.

245.title: LWLG — Ren
245.body: Lightwave Logic is too risky to recommend unless something material changes.

246.title: DDOG — Ren
246.body:
AI should increase telemetry ingestion, lift renewals and reinforce Datadog's broad integrations.

OpenAI's move to ClickHouse also warns that log costs can become burdensome at hyperscale. Broad demand growth can coexist with the largest customers seeking cheaper alternatives.

247.title: IREN — Ren
247.body:
IREN's Microsoft arrangement appears comparatively protected from higher GPU prices: Dell financing and Microsoft's prepayment are said to cover approximately 95% of its hardware cost.

The new deals under discussion have estimated paybacks of roughly two years.

248.title: DGXX — Ren
248.body:
Digi Power X is a speculative bet on building a Cerebras colocation campus on schedule.

A ten-year $1.1 billion contract, expandable to $2.5 billion, supports upside. The first 40 MW Alabama phase targets December 2026; another 25 MW still needs financing.

The company remains loss-making and exposed to crypto. Cerebras reported a $145.9 million operating loss and got 86% of 2025 revenue from two UAE entities. A second tenant and early GPU-service revenue could broaden demand.

249.title: TTMI — Ren
249.body:
PCB suppliers offer lower-risk, lower-return AI hardware exposure. Unimicron is held; TTM Technologies is under consideration.

Morgan Stanley estimates PCB value per AI system could rise 233% between generations. Unimicron has an estimated 18-22% AI-server PCB share, 8% sequential Q1 growth and 18% gross margin.

TTM's Q1 revenue rose 30% to $846m, with data centers and networking at 36% of sales. Q2 guidance was $930m-$970m. Elite Material supplies laminate rather than finished boards.

250.title: XSAT:SHT B — Ren
250.body:
Smart High-Tech remains a speculative holding through 2030, capped at 2%, with no buying or selling planned.

After a 30% daily gain, a target of one million thermal pads monthly supports expansion expectations. A May 25 delivery, customer approval, a $300,000 prepayment under a $5m 2026 framework and Henkel distribution add support. Nvidia orders remain unconfirmed. Production, financing, dilution and governance are risks.

251.title: GLW — Ren
251.body:
Corning has pricing power as North American fiber demand grows an estimated 22-25%, against supply growth of 12-19%.

Lead times have reached twenty weeks for large buyers and up to a year for smaller customers.

Demand includes a multibillion-dollar, multi-year Amazon agreement, Meta's $6 billion January agreement and two unnamed first-quarter hyperscaler deals. A May Nvidia initiative targets a tenfold increase in U.S. optical-connectivity capacity.

252.title: XSAT:SMOL — Ren
252.body:
The full Smoltek position remains held after the stock gain since the call fell from about 100% to about 30%.

Decisions depend on catalysts rather than price alone, with trimming planned into future strength. Dilution limits conviction and explains the initial 1% allocation; the key commercial catalysts are still ahead.

253.title: BRUN — Ren
253.body:
BRUN remains a long with an expectation above $45. Backlog growth, the take-or-pay contract and Dell financing make the business attractive.

About 4.88 million shares are estimated to have unlocked. The larger share-supply risk is November 8.

254.title: IPWR — Ren
254.body:
Ideal Power is a speculative holding in bidirectional switches for fast protection in 800V AI racks. Prototype tests must become repeat orders; production revenue is still prospective.

A May 14 letter of intent targets an unnamed US cloud customer's prototype in late 2026, with possible 2027 production. Claimed switching losses are one-quarter of conventional designs. Over $16m cash, no debt and outsourced manufacturing help, but total loss remains possible.

255.title: AMPG — Ren
255.body:
AmpliTech is a small, high-risk holding whose radio, AI-network and quantum orders must become H2 sales.

Firm backlog exceeds $20m versus $118m in letters of intent and $50m annual guidance. One customer supplies about half of sales; reporting weaknesses add risk. Full rights exercise could raise $49.5m and lift shares from 25.2m to 34.2m, or about 38.9m with options and the equity plan. Projected exercise dates are July 18 and November 20.

256.title: 011070.KS — Ren
256.body:
LG Innotek is held for cameras and advanced chip substrates at about 13x estimated FY2026 earnings. Packaging sales rose 16%; AI substrate expansion could tighten older packaging supply.

Over 80% Apple exposure ties demand to iPhone sales and tariffs. A 500% year-to-date rally and 60% weekly gain make a 20%-30% pullback plausible. The ambition is for packaging to match cameras in five years; glass-substrate revenue remains prospective.

257.title: CIEN / LITE / COHR — Ren
257.body: Rosenblatt expects Ciena data-center interconnect and scale-across orders to reaccelerate. Coherent Lite inside data centers offers a 2027 opportunity. The analyst target is $720.

258.title: COHR — Ren
258.body:
Coherent reported $2.05 billion revenue, up 34%, with InP laser production growing approximately 80% annually and bookings extending into calendar 2028.

Those results support the bullish optical supply-chain case.

259.title: PLTR — Ren
259.body: Palantir's Ontology connects fragmented data to real business objects and relationships, making it relevant to enterprise AI learning systems. More organizations should recognize that value.

260.title: 440110.KQ / SIMO — Ren
260.body:
Nvidia's proposed CMX inference-storage tier could benefit SSD-controller and architecture suppliers as well as NAND producers.

Silicon Motion and FADU offer exposure to large-block, read-heavy, multi-tenant workloads that need power-efficient SSDs.

261.title: CCXI — Ren
261.body:
CCXI's proposed merger with Agility Robotics offers a speculative way to invest in warehouse robots.

Agility's Digit robots already operate at customer sites, and the company has multiyear orders. Closing the merger would bring more funding, but the business remains unprofitable and investors face dilution. This is a trading position, not a core long-term holding.

262.title: FN / LITE — Ren
262.body:
Fabrinet data-center growth and capacity expansion support a favorable outlook.

Rosenblatt cites sequential Nvidia growth, new Amazon and Lumentum business, and an on-track capacity ramp. Its $750 target compares with shares near $480.

263.title: VIAV — Ren
263.body: Viavi selling on indium-phosphide supply fears looks misplaced: Rosenblatt sees no exposure to that issue. Its $70 target compares with shares near $41.

264.title: ANET — Ren
264.body:
Arista relationships with Meta, Microsoft and Oracle, plus expanding Google and Anthropic business, support further growth.

Rosenblatt expects revenue growth above 30% into the second half and suggests Google could become a 10% customer in 2026.

265.title: PENG — Ren
265.body:
Penguin remains held after a 33% fall. Quarterly sales rose 48% to $479m; memory more than doubled to $275m, and computing outside major clouds rose 81%.

Business and government customers support growth, but year-to-date operating cash flow was just $11m and relied on later supplier payments. Investment sales flattered profit. High memory prices threaten margins and orders; the 2027 optical-memory proposal is unproven. Major-cloud spending could peak in 2028.

266.title: INDI — Ren
266.body:
Indie is a small holding at $3.70 as car-camera chips win Unitree and Agibot robotics business. Built-in memory helps amid shortages.

Its $149m cash covers about four quarters. A $135m Wuxi sale needs approval; a sensor acquisition is proposed. Share-based pay equals 28% of revenue. Core break-even needs quarterly sales near $58m, 46% above guidance. The estimated 18-month path assumes 30% growth without delays.

267.title: CRWV / NBIS — Ren
267.body:
CoreWeave is repricing new contracts about 25% higher with better margins, but rising GPU costs threaten capacity already sold cheaply under long-term contracts, particularly Microsoft.

GPU ownership, more than $35 billion of debt and debt-funded expansion make it more exposed than Nebius despite pricing power on new business.

268.title: HUT — Ren
268.body:
Hut 8 looks attractive after a report of a $35 billion Anthropic-Lambda computing agreement.

The Wall Street Journal report, relayed by wallstengine, describes Nvidia supplying chips and leasing Hut 8's 700-megawatt Texas campus. Existing campus leases run fifteen years. The roughly $20 billion figure for Hut 8's facilities is separate from the $35 billion cloud agreement.

269.title: SNOW — Ren
269.body:
AI is accelerating Snowflake's sales but making workloads more costly.

Product revenue rose 37% to $1.49bn, its third acceleration; management attributes about half the acceleration to AI. Annual revenue guidance rose from $5.84bn to $6.07bn and operating margin from 13.5% to 14.5%. Product gross-margin guidance fell to 74%. Contracted future revenue grew 30%, slower than sales. Shares rose 22% after hours.

270.title: JBL — Ren
270.body: Jabil reported $8.8 billion quarterly revenue and raised next-quarter guidance to $9.2-$10.0 billion. Its higher AI revenue outlook supports continued demand for optical manufacturing and suppliers.

271.title: STM / POWI — Ren
271.body: STMicroelectronics is a preferred power-semiconductor supplier because it controls multiple stages of silicon-carbide production. This supports its place in the AI power supply chain.

272.title: POWI — Ren
272.body: Power Integrations' InnoSwitch products offer efficient conversion, fewer components and reliability in the AI power supply chain. These advantages support the investment view.

273.title: ADTN — Ren
273.body: Adtran remains a promising investment candidate after further research, with more company developments anticipated.

274.title: MSFT — Jerry Capital
274.body: OpenAI could disrupt Microsoft's productivity business despite strong Azure growth.

275.title: ASML — Jerry Capital
275.body:
An AI-generated assessment framed the Chinese scanner as a possible substitute for older immersion tools.

Production qualification, reliability and manufacturing scale remained unproven, limiting the case for a competitive breakthrough against ASML.

276.title: FOUR — Jerry Capital
276.body:
Converting acquired payment volumes creates an opportunity for Shift4, but switching costs and price concessions can limit returns.

An AI-assisted assessment also highlighted capital intensity and operating complexity in fragmented markets.

277.title: TDG — Jerry Capital
277.body: TransDigm looks attractive because management focuses on increasing shareholder wealth.

278.title: V / MA — Jerry Capital
278.body: Visa, Mastercard and Ant International's Know-Your-Agent framework supported the networks' continuing role in agent payments. Merchant checkout and Shop Pay interfaces still faced disruption risk.

279.title: CSU.TO — Jerry Capital
279.body: Aging private-equity software holdings and blocked exits could increase Constellation's acquisition opportunities. Its valuation was expected to move back toward a 3% free-cash-flow yield.

280.title: SPGI — Jerry Capital
280.body:
Capital IQ Pro contributed less than 6% of S&P Global revenue, while early AI-ready data renewals brought reported uplifts of 35-45%.

Acquisitions faced a higher return hurdle relative to returning capital to shareholders.

281.title: CRM / GPN — Jerry Capital
281.body: Continued software acquisitions could worsen Salesforce's valuation problems. Global Payments' depressed multiple offered a warning.

282.title: DHR — Jerry Capital
282.body: Danaher may be too large for acquisitions to restore strong growth, even if it buys businesses more effectively. Other compounders look more attractive until growth and returns improve.

283.title: INTU — Jerry Capital
283.body:
Tax disruption needed evidence from filed returns, more complex tax situations, free pricing and declines in TurboTax paid users or pricing.

If TurboTax revenue per user broke, QuickBooks would need to carry the stock.

284.title: PYPL — Jerry Capital
284.body: A potential PayPal takeover could require divesting Braintree or part of the European business as regulatory remedies.

285.title: ZTS — Jerry Capital
285.body:
Zoetis spent about $4.4 billion on repurchases at an average price roughly 60% above the later market price, leaving about $1.3 billion authorized as the outlook weakened.

The purchases reduced shares beyond offsetting dilution.

286.title: MORN — Jerry Capital
286.body:
ChatGPT for Financial Services uses PitchBook's database instead of building a replacement.

AI could therefore bring more demand for Morningstar's data even if customers stop using some of its software screens.

287.title: TTWO — Jerry Capital
287.body: A GTA V mod used for drone training suggested potential applications beyond ordinary entertainment for Take-Two.

288.title: TTD — Jerry Capital
288.body: Neutrality alone would not compensate for weaker data or inventory access at The Trade Desk. A platform with better inputs could win despite conflicts of interest.

289.title: AAPL — Jerry Capital
289.body:
An AI-assisted assessment placed Apple behind other customers at TSMC and memory suppliers, with difficulty securing A19 Pro, A18 Pro and memory.

Reduced supply priority could push margins down from their peak.

290.title: NKE — Q-Cap
290.body: Nike was down 72% since 2022 but still traded at a stated 30 times earnings on April 1. The drawdown had not made the valuation clearly attractive.

291.title: SNAP — Q-Cap
291.body: Snap's new $2,195 augmented-reality glasses raised further concerns about capital allocation and shareholder returns.

292.title: INTC — Q-Cap
292.body: Intel appeared to show a breakout pattern 26 years in the making.

293.title: AAPL — Q-Cap
293.body: Apple had fifteen years to develop Siri into an AI leader but failed to capitalize on that head start. A prospective OpenAI and Qualcomm phone could challenge its smartphone dominance.

294.title: 000660.KS — Q-Cap
294.body:
SK hynix was up 1,570% over three years yet traded at a cited 4.5 times next-twelve-month earnings, with 80% EBITDA margins.

Staying on the sidelines was preferred: the shares could be deeply undervalued or exposed to a major semiconductor crash.

295.title: GME — Q-Cap
295.body: GameStop's proposed eBay purchase could dilute existing shareholders because the financing discussion appears to leave a funding gap above $10 billion. GameStop has not confirmed that estimate, and the proposal already includes payment in shares.

296.title: UBER — Q-Cap
296.body: Uber appeared to be building sustainable free cash flow, with mobility demand holding up surprisingly well despite wartime oil-price pressure. This was an initial assessment ahead of deeper research.

297.title: AXON — Q-Cap
297.body: Replacing police officers with humanoid robots would face resistance to job displacement and a cited 80% police-unionization rate.

298.title: FSLY / RDDT — Q-Cap
298.body: Fastly's ContentGuard can help websites such as Reddit detect AI scraping and either block it or charge for access. Customer interest and tighter crawler rules could support Fastly demand.

299.title: BRK-B — Q-Cap
299.body: Berkshire offers portfolio diversification because it can move differently from the broader market.

300.title: SPCX — Q-Cap
300.body: Some SpaceX IPO shares were received. Nasdaq 100 inclusion flows could push its market value above Nvidia's, even though the valuation looked irrational.

301.title: OPEN — Q-Cap
301.body: Investing for future assets can be legitimate, but it does not alter GAAP earnings or justify redefining profitability for public-market investors.

302.title: GOOG — Q-Cap
302.body: Google Cloud's cited 82% growth was encouraging.

303.title: PYPL — Q-Cap
303.body: A reverse merger was uncertain because Stripe might have little appetite for a public listing. It did not appear to need the money and was described as strongly cash-flow positive.

304.title: V — Q-Cap
304.body: Visa looked attractive for patient ownership as part of an oligopoly with a cited 70% EBITDA margin.

305.title: CSU.TO — Q-Cap
305.body:
Constellation Software reportedly traded at a lower price-to-earnings ratio than Royal Bank of Canada for the first time since the 2009 financial crisis.

That valuation gap looked difficult to justify.

306.title: FIX — Q-Cap
306.body: Comfort Systems USA traded at 41.1 times forward earnings versus Nvidia at 20.8 times. That premium looked questionable given Nvidia's central role in enabling the AI buildout.

307.title: GEV / VRT / CEG / ETN — Q-Cap
307.body: GE Vernova, Vertiv, Constellation Energy and Eaton are preferred ways to invest in the power shortages facing AI data centers.

308.title: DLO — Q-Cap
308.body: dLocal's emerging-market payments opportunity looked demanding relative to potentially easier investments. The effort required needed to justify its opportunity cost.

309.title: FICO — Q-Cap
309.body: FICO offered a short-term rebound trade after a technically excessive decline, with potentially larger buybacks providing support. The long-term business case remained less attractive.

310.title: GLW — Traderstewie
310.body: Corning's reversal from the 50-day moving average and inside-day candle offered a setup for renewed buying over the next few sessions, with a $160 target.

311.title: NKE / MU — Traderstewie
311.body: Nike had become a major market disappointment, with business conditions less favorable than Micron's.

312.title: VRT — Traderstewie
312.body: Vertiv has reached a new high while much of the market is falling. Its AI infrastructure business and strong relative performance make it worth watching.

313.title: RKLB — Traderstewie
313.body: Rocket Lab's earnings gap on exceptionally heavy volume makes it a technical leader.

314.title: LWLG — Traderstewie
314.body: Strong buying volume made Lightwave Logic's wedge and flag pattern particularly attractive.

315.title: OPEN — Traderstewie
315.body: A move above $6 on strong volume would improve Opendoor's setup.

316.title: VSAT — Traderstewie
316.body: Recent volume is a concern. If Viasat does not bounce promptly, the assessment expects a possible break below the 20-day moving average and a test of the 50-day average.

317.title: INTC — Traderstewie
317.body: Intel's six-session pullback is controlled and occurs on lighter volume after an earnings-related advance. Renewed buying is expected, with a $130 target.

318.title: FIVN — Traderstewie
318.body: Five9's May 1 earnings gap and consolidation have led to a strong upward move. @kkernttb identified the setup.

319.title: GRPN — Traderstewie
319.body: Groupon's chart was improving and appeared to be forming a base. A breakout above $19 resistance could trigger stronger upside.

320.title: AKAM — Traderstewie
320.body: Akamai's two-week consolidation after an earnings gap and improving volume suggested a possible move toward new highs, with targets of $175 and $185.

321.title: FLYW — Traderstewie
321.body: Flywire's consolidation after an earnings-related gap offered a favorable technical setup, identified by @kkernttb.

322.title: MXL — Traderstewie
322.body: MaxLinear's improving relative strength supported the moving-average rebound setup.

323.title: QUBT — Traderstewie
323.body: Quantum Computing reversed with relative strength, supporting its bullish setup and the possibility of a squeeze.

324.title: SMR — Traderstewie
324.body: NuScale's possible failed breakout could provide a better base for renewed upside toward the end of the week.

325.title: CLS — Traderstewie
325.body: Celestica's recovery through its 50-day moving average looked constructive, with targets of $420 and $440.

326.title: IWM — Traderstewie
326.body: IWM reached a new high while the Nasdaq retraced 7% from its highs, demonstrating relative strength.

327.title: XLV — Traderstewie
327.body: XLV rebounded from its 20-day moving-average setup. The better entry was the previous day, making chasing the current move unattractive.

328.title: TRV — Traderstewie
328.body: Travelers' test of its 20-day exponential moving average offered a favorable pullback entry setup.

329.title: GRMN — Traderstewie
329.body: Garmin is showing constructive price action after its earnings gap and looks like an emerging technical leader.

330.title: AVGO — Traderstewie
330.body: Broadcom was becoming short-term oversold at key support. Nvidia's earnings could provide a catalyst for a bounce.

331.title: WDC / AMD — Traderstewie
331.body: Western Digital's consolidation resembled AMD's. The pattern was less tidy but still offered a strong chance of an upside breakout.

332.title: NVDA — Traderstewie
332.body: Nvidia's strong upward gap after earnings was a positive technical signal.

333.title: CRWV — Traderstewie
333.body: CoreWeave is expected to rise after a few more days of consolidation.

334.title: ANET — Traderstewie
334.body: Arista Networks had consolidated for several weeks near its 20-day moving average. Renewed upside toward $220-$230 was expected.

335.title: FIG — mon
335.body: Claude Design threatens Figma by letting users create prototypes and design materials through conversation.

336.title: NRGV — mon
336.body:
Energy Vault's thesis remains intact despite a stop-loss exit at $4.

Reported revenue growth exceeds 150% year over year, backlog is $1.35 billion, up 108%, and more than 80% of backlog represents recurring revenue. Expansion in Japan and the US continues, with a year-end total-cash target of $150 million to $200 million.

337.title: CLSK — mon
337.body: CleanSpark is worth watching for a first major cloud customer. A signed agreement could help it earn money from its power assets, as Hut 8 aims to do.

338.title: MRVL / POET — mon
338.body: Marvell's optical capabilities and Celestial AI acquisition make the POET order cancellation look favorable for Marvell. The confidentiality-breach explanation remains an interpretation, not Marvell's stated motive.

339.title: TGEN — mon
339.body:
Tecogen's gas-electric chiller can shift cooling load away from constrained grid electricity, potentially freeing power for AI servers.

The Vertiv demonstration purchase is an early validation route, but large-scale customer adoption is still needed. A pullback is expected after a greater-than-200% rally in under two months, despite continued ownership.

340.title: POET — mon
340.body:
POET looks attractive if the confidentiality breach was a management failure rather than a problem with the technology.

Its shares have rebounded 211.67%, but a restoration of the canceled Marvell orders is unconfirmed.

341.title: INV — mon
341.body: Accelsius is the main reason to own Innventure. A separate listing or spin-off could make the cooling business easier to value, but none has been announced.

342.title: ENPH — mon
342.body:
Enphase's solid-state transformer could power AI racks if it meets its efficiency and reliability goals.

Pilots are expected in 2027 and volume shipments in 2028. Successful delivery could bring the shares back to a triple-digit price.

343.title: FTC.L — mon
343.body:
Filtronic's high-frequency amplifiers and reported SpaceX order book support a growth case from FY2027.

New space customers could reduce concentration and a SpaceX IPO could lift attention to suppliers. No position is held yet; new customers are prospective, not completed wins.

344.title: AIRJ — mon
344.body:
AirJoule was bought about two weeks before the May 28 post, with a reported 28% gain.

The technology aims to use waste heat to remove moisture, produce water and reduce cooling energy. Commercial revenue is not expected to become meaningful until 2027, and pilot performance still must translate into large-scale customer adoption.

345.title: AMZN — mon
345.body:
Amazon Prime combines recurring membership fees with benefits that encourage more shopping. Delivery, entertainment and other services build loyalty beyond the subscription itself.

Spotify is part of customers' daily routines, supporting repeat subscription revenue. Costco offers value that encourages membership renewals and loyal shopping. These recurring customer relationships make all three businesses attractive.

source.label: If you’re new to investing, start with Subscription-based businesses.

346.title: OUST — mon
346.body: Ouster's lidar helps robots detect obstacles, map their surroundings and respond. More robots could mean more customers for those sensors.

347.title: IREN / NBIS / CRWV — mon
347.body:
OpenAI still needs more computing, even after buying capacity a year ago that its CFO says is now worth three to five times as much.

That shortage supports investing in IREN, Nebius and CoreWeave, which rent access to AI chips.

348.title: CAT — mon
348.body: Caterpillar remains favored as an indirect beneficiary of AI infrastructure, with its dividend noted alongside the prior generator-demand case.

349.title: GOOGL — mon
349.body:
Alphabet is presented as an indirect way to participate in SpaceX, Anthropic and Waymo through its ownership interests.

That route avoids relying on a direct purchase of those businesses, although the value to Alphabet shareholders depends on the size and terms of the stakes and the rest of Alphabet's operations.

350.title: ENHA — mon
350.body:
Enhanced Group could convert Enhanced Games viewers into repeat telehealth customers for peptides, weight-loss and hormone treatments. Viewers still need to become paying patients who stay.

The first purchase is complete. The plan is to build toward 10% of the portfolio over coming months, not an achieved allocation. Tenfold upside is contemplated without a supplied valuation model.

351.title: DRAM — mon
351.body: Micron management does not yet see when supply will catch demand. DRAM is a preferred way to invest in that shortage.

352.title: ASTS — mon
352.body:
AST SpaceMobile needs to launch satellites and make the network usable before substantial service revenue can follow.

Operator relationships and government awards suggest demand. Japan's selection is described as preliminary at this point.

353.title: KEEL — mon
353.body:
Keel's roughly 2.2-gigawatt development pipeline and existing grid connections create potential value, but the valuation gap with peers remains because it has not secured a large cloud customer.

The pipeline is not all operating capacity, and the three-lease year-end goal remains a key test.

354.title: SPGI — mon
354.body:
S&P Global appears inexpensive as revenue has nearly doubled over five years while the shares have gained roughly 5%.

The June 20 assessment describes the stock as down 19% year to date and near a five-year valuation low, with market attention diverted toward AI.

355.title: MA / V — mon
355.body: Visa also looks attractive, but Mastercard is preferred after its larger year-to-date decline.

356.title: NFLX — mon
356.body: Netflix looks worth buying after its large decline because subscribers and earnings are still growing. The business has not weakened as much as the share price.

357.title: MSFT — mon
357.body:
Microsoft can slow CPU and GPU additions or use capacity in its own applications if demand changes.

That flexibility supports the resilience of its AI strategy, while current customer demand is reported to exceed available capacity.

358.title: META — mon
358.body: Meta aims to double its AI computing capacity to around 14 GW by 2027. Its own demand is likely to absorb further infrastructure investment.

359.title: UBER — mon
359.body:
Uber's fast earnings growth contrasts with a share price well below its peak.

The June 20 argument favors accumulating the business near the bottom of its recent range while investors are preoccupied with other sectors.

360.title: RDDT — mon
360.body: Reddit's Q2 revenue, EBITDA and free cash flow all grew faster than expected, making the post-earnings selloff a buying opportunity.

361.title: PENG — mon
361.body: Penguin's memory systems give AI processors more room for data and reduce waiting. More customer adoption would bring sales. After the large share-price rise, it remains a smaller position rather than a core holding.

362.title: NUAI — mon
362.body:
NUAI offers speculative upside from its West Texas assets and on-site power opportunity.

Securing a power agreement, tenant and revenue could raise its valuation, so the investment accepts the risk of buying before those milestones.

363.title: AMZN — mon
363.body: AWS revenue and profit growth suggest Amazon's AI spending is starting to pay off. The shares rose as investors responded to those results.

364.title: SIVE.ST / AAOI / LITE / COHR / AXTI / GFS — mon
364.body:
As AI clusters expand, electrical connections face greater power, heat and signal-loss constraints.

Optical links address part of that problem, supporting research into Sivers, AAOI, Lumentum, Coherent, AXT and GlobalFoundries after their share-price declines. The companies occupy different parts of the chain and are not interchangeable exposures.

media.alt: SIVE.ST / AAOI / LITE / COHR / AXTI / GFS / LYTE quoted-context image

365.title: NBIS — mon
365.body:
Nebius can use large contracts and customer prepayments to fund expansion while retaining some capacity for customers willing to pay for immediate access.

This combination offers growth and pricing flexibility, provided the company delivers.

366.title: CIFR / IREN — mon
366.body:
IREN and Cipher could benefit as Texas makes new grid-connected data-center development harder.

Existing approved power positions become more valuable, but each site's actual interconnection agreements and approvals still matter.

367.title: RIOT — mon
367.body:
RIOT's announced 191-megawatt AI lease offers attractive economics: $9.1 billion over 20 years and potentially $16.1 billion with extensions.

Expected net operating income is $7.3-8.2 billion over the initial term, or roughly $365-411 million annually. The first 96 megawatts are targeted for December 2027 and full delivery for June 2028. The tenant is unnamed; Anthropic is only a conjecture. A separate Corsicana proposal remains a letter of intent.

368.title: CRWV — mon
368.body:
Reported renewals for older GPUs challenge assumptions of rapid economic obsolescence.

That may support collateral values and financing, but CoreWeave's contracted book leaves much of its repricing opportunity in renewals and future agreements.

source.label: #1: My thoughts on NVDA raising prices.

369.title: WYFI — mon
369.body:
WhiteFiber's proposed convertible raise could create a buying opportunity after the sharp share-price decline, depending on final terms.

Expansion requires substantial funding relative to the company's size, leaving dilution and financing costs important to the investment outcome.

370.title: BE — mon
370.body: Bloom Energy's on-site generation can power data centers without waiting years for grid capacity. That gives it a competitive advantage while AI electricity demand grows.

371.title: SKHY — mon
371.body:
SK hynix's value depends on how it uses the cash from AI demand, as well as on memory prices.

Buybacks, new production and acquisitions could create value beyond the current cycle. Nvidia offers an example of reinvesting that cash, not a direct valuation match.

372.title: UMAC — mon
372.body: Tariffs on foreign drones could help Unusual Machines sell more domestic products. The benefit depends on which products qualify and whether customers buy them profitably.

373.title: PNGAF — mon
373.body: Precision Peptide's patch products and planned rollout are interesting as a different delivery format. The shares are unavailable on the brokerage platform being used.

374.title: KRKNF — mon
374.body: Kraken can supply sonar and batteries to competing underwater-vehicle makers. That is attractive because it does not need one manufacturer to dominate, provided orders arrive and are delivered.

source.label: The 7 bets on where the world is heading over the next decade.

375.title: IBRX — mon
375.body:
ImmunityBio's approved bladder-cancer treatment and existing revenue provide a starting point for expansion into larger oncology indications.

The upside depends on clinical results, making this a particularly risky long-term investment.

source.label: The 7 bets on where the world is heading over the next decade.

376.title: MU — mon
376.body:
Micron's long customer agreements make demand more predictable but can cap selling prices.

Packaging and other costs rising under those caps would squeeze margins. Deliveries and contract terms matter as much as the broader memory demand.

377.title: 005930.KS — mon
377.body:
Samsung could recover after its high-bandwidth-memory setbacks.

The guide reports that HBM4 passed Nvidia and AMD testing, began shipping in early 2026 and reached prices comparable with SK hynix. Analysts expect market share above 30%, but that has not yet been achieved. Other Samsung businesses also affect the stock.

378.title: SNDK — mon
378.body:
SanDisk and Kioxia make NAND flash used in fast storage.

AI demand and tight supply support prices, with their 2026 production described as effectively committed. Seagate and Western Digital instead supply lower-cost hard-drive storage.

SanDisk's high-bandwidth-flash project with SK hynix could add another product in the future, but it does not yet produce established revenue.

379.title: 2802.T — mon
379.body:
Ajinomoto's build-up film, or ABF, is a difficult-to-replace insulating material for advanced chip packages.

The guide reports a roughly 30% price increase effective in Q3 2026 as supply tightens. This could benefit the materials business, although it remains a small part of the wider food company.

380.title: SIVE.ST — mon
380.body:
Sivers could win more laser business as AI networks expand. Customer testing must become repeat orders and profitable production. The disclosed position is very small.

The laser business is still loss-making, while the valuation already assumes growth. New financing helps fund expansion, but potential deals and technology partnerships are not yet sales.

381.title: LITE — mon
381.body:
Lumentum is a more established optical company, with factories, approved products and strong reported margins.

More orders could let profits grow faster than sales as those factories fill. Its high share price still assumes substantial growth.

382.title: NOK — Art of Speculation
382.body:
Nokia's July results support the AI-network opportunity, but guidance stayed unchanged.

Production capacity remains the bottleneck: stronger orders can take longer to become revenue when deliveries are constrained. Higher output and shipments are the next tests.

383.title: AAOI — Ren
383.body:
The large AAOI holding remains as Texas factories expand.

A 388,000-square-foot project takes Houston space toward 900,000 square feet, targeting 700,000 transceivers monthly and about 350% more laser capacity by end-2027. A first volume 1.6T order supports demand. Revenue guidance exceeds $1.1bn for 2026 versus $456m in 2025. Delivery still depends on finishing the factories; the shares remain volatile.

384.title: MU — Art of Speculation
384.body: Micron is losing momentum near resistance and risks a pullback. The rebound depends on holding moving-average support and breaking through resistance.

385.title: GOOG — 3X Long Labubu
385.body:
The first few quarters of the AI-search transition were expected to be neutral or even negative for Google's overall advertising revenue.

The longer-term view remained optimistic because customers needed education and the models, systems and ad relevance needed iteration.

386.title: AEHR — Traderstewie
386.body: Aehr Test Systems revisited its earlier low, held that level and turned higher. The reversal supports the rebound setup and increases risk for traders betting on another decline.

387.title: QCOM — Art of Speculation
387.body:
Qualcomm's custom chips, cache technology and chip-to-chip connections offer more routes to data-center revenue.

Details from JPMorgan's hardware and semiconductor forum strengthen the product case, but customers still need to buy in meaningful volume.

388.title: GLW — Art of Speculation
388.body:
Cloud customers reserving Corning's optical capacity offer a clearer path to future sales from AI data centers.

Multiyear partnerships support the demand case. Higher earnings and a stronger valuation still depend on those commitments becoming delivered business.

Corning is several years away from earning meaningful revenue from glass chip packaging. Existing optical contracts concern a different product business.

389.title: RDDT / META / GOOG / PINS — Q-Cap
389.body:
Reddit could have substantial upside if U.S. revenue per user moves toward Pinterest's level.

Meta, YouTube and Pinterest show the monetization range, although their audiences and businesses differ.

390.title: TLT — 3X Long Labubu
390.body: TLT calls remained exposed to a decline in long-term yields, but rising real yields overwhelmed lower inflation expectations and reversed the initial bond-market reaction.

391.title: SKHY — 3X Long Labubu
391.body: SKHY's widening premium over Korean common shares made partial profit-taking preferable. Further ADR purchases should wait for the premium to settle; the estimated 25%-35% premium remains uncertain.

392.title: NOK — Ren
392.body:
Long Nokia for its underappreciated optical assets.

The Allentown expansion provides exposure to AI optical packaging and U.S. supply-chain investment, though the factory is small relative to Nokia's overall business.

393.title: MU — Traderstewie
393.body: Micron is consolidating near its 50-day moving average, creating a possible upside breakout this week.

394.title: SMH — Traderstewie
394.body: SMH fills its opening gap and immediately reverses higher. A few more constructive sessions are expected to support a breakout from the bottoming pattern.

395.title: SPCX — Cathie Wood
395.body: An Anthropic deal could turn Colossus from a loss-making operation into a profitable supplier of rented AI computing. Annual revenue from that activity is estimated at $5-$6 billion or more.

396.title: INTC — Art of Speculation
396.body:
Tight TSMC capacity could bring foundry work to Intel.

The Information reported a Google order for more than three million TPU chips for delivery in 2028 and Nvidia's evaluation of 18A. Commercial production remains a future milestone.

397.title: RKLB — Art of Speculation
397.body: Rocket Lab may have topped at $150. A rebound from around $100 is expected to form a lower high at $120-$130, reducing the anticipated pre-IPO upside.

398.title: ALAB / CRDO — Art of Speculation
398.body:
Astera Labs is preferred to Credo because its switches, telemetry, diagnostics and software integration strengthen the business case.

The shares could reach $360-$370 within a few months, with $450-$460 still forecast for year-end. Buying after the rally is not recommended.

399.title: AMD — Art of Speculation
399.body: For AMD's 24-36 month CPU opportunity, the preferred entry is a confirmed retest of the breakout around $290-$300.

400.title: BE — Art of Speculation
400.body:
Bloom Energy's agreement with Nebius supports demand for on-site generation as grid connections and permits delay data-center deployment.

The contract is worth up to approximately $2.6 billion and is expected to provide around 250 MW of guaranteed capacity and 328 MW of installed capacity across three phases.

401.title: USO — Art of Speculation
401.body:
After crude's sharp rally, oil resistance at $103-$108 favors gradually building a short position in USO.

Higher fuel prices could increase pressure for geopolitical compromise around the November midterms, potentially reversing oil and bond yields.

402.title: CRCL — Art of Speculation
402.body:
Programmable AI-agent payments and wider USDC use could improve Circle's network economics, but valuation is high and investment spending is compressing profit.

The plan is to wait one to two months, build over three to twelve months and hold one to two years. USDC, Circle shares and a possible Arc token provide distinct exposures.

403.title: IREN — Art of Speculation
403.body:
Power access, land, grid connections and construction cannot expand as quickly as GPU production, supporting IREN's infrastructure position.

A higher valuation requires growth in backlog, operating capacity and recurring revenue, alongside lower financing costs.

404.title: NBIS — Art of Speculation
404.body:
Nebius could earn more from the same AI chips by improving the software that runs them.

That work needs to be repeated for each new chip and model. IREN offers a different advantage through its early access to power, so owning both would cover two different customer needs.

405.title: BTC — Art of Speculation
405.body:
Bitcoin has reached $59,200, clearing liquidity below $60,000.

The bounce remains weak despite extremely oversold readings. Gradual spot accumulation is worth considering for diversification, while a reversal remains unconfirmed.

406.title: LITE — Art of Speculation
406.body: Pump and narrow-linewidth lasers could drive Lumentum's earnings growth if planned 2027 capacity comes online on schedule.

407.title: SPY — Art of Speculation
407.body: Weak breadth, fading volume and crowded semiconductor positions leave the S&P 500 vulnerable near 7,200, especially if the Fed is hawkish. Bitcoin's lower high around $79,000 adds caution. AI-driven job reductions could also pose a future demand risk.

408.title: AVGO — Art of Speculation
408.body:
Broadcom's custom-chip leadership, long customer relationships and software cash flow support a relatively steady AI investment, provided hyperscaler spending continues.

Management's prospective AI revenue supports growth, but a two- or threefold share-price gain looks difficult. Nokia's business is not yet familiar enough to assess.

409.title: LEU — Art of Speculation
409.body: Centrus Energy's domestic enriched-fuel capability, government awards and backlog support the business case. Commercial delivery and reactor deployment remain essential.

410.title: CRWV — Art of Speculation
410.body: CoreWeave is worth holding only with controlled position size. Heavy debt and annual capital spending could leave it among the first companies affected by financial stress, despite its backlog.

411.title: COHR / LITE — Art of Speculation
411.body:
Coherent's integration from indium phosphide wafers through lasers and optical modules improves supply control.

A successful six-inch wafer ramp could lower unit costs and raise margins. Competition with Lumentum remains material.

412.title: ORCL — Art of Speculation
412.body:
Oracle's one-to-three-month outlook is neutral to bearish, favoring entries at $160-$170.

The one-to-two-year target remains above $300. Negative free cash flow, financing needs, thinner rental margins and OpenAI concentration temper the strong backlog case.

413.title: NOW — Art of Speculation
413.body: ServiceNow could reach $140-$150 if it holds above $125. The shares have recovered the earlier $105 area and stand above the 50-day moving average.

414.title: NVDA — Art of Speculation
414.body:
Nvidia is one of five preferred AI investments over the next one to three years and ranks in the top infrastructure group.

Business quality, valuation, stability and growth support the ranking; it does not imply the largest share-price gain.

415.title: CRWV — 3X Long Labubu
415.body:
CoreWeave was not intended as a long-term holding.

Because of volatility, the preferred trade used three- to six-month out-of-the-money calls, with additions at estimated support levels and a stop if all those levels failed.

416.title: CBRS — 3X Long Labubu
416.body: Cerebras's lack of dependence on high-bandwidth memory is attractive, but the following day's investor event warrants caution.

417.title: CRDO / AMZN / MRVL — 3X Long Labubu
417.body: Small Credo and Marvell positions were added after hours following strong Amazon earnings and its explanation of investment returns. No Amazon position was held.

418.title: AVGO — 3X Long Labubu
418.body: Reports of lower TPU output expectations and possible AMD involvement in a future Google TPU project may explain Broadcom's selloff.

419.title: NVDA — 3X Long Labubu
419.body:
OpenAI's joint design of models, frameworks and hardware is promising longer term, but is not expected to outperform Nvidia's stack for at least three years because of talent and priority constraints.

Its nearer role is a backup and a bargaining tool with Nvidia.

420.title: ORCL — 3X Long Labubu
420.body: Oracle's strong relative performance is encouraging because rising rates would normally pressure its credit-default-swap pricing.

421.title: NOK — Manchurius Hao
421.body:
Nokia's main valuation test is Network Infrastructure, especially optical and IP orders, AI and cloud sales, book-to-bill and margins.

Continued growth could justify a higher group valuation; deterioration would create value-trap risk. AI-RAN adds a longer-term option.

422.title: MRAM — Manchurius Hao
422.body:
Everspin's opportunity lies in defense, aerospace and high-reliability electronics that preserve state through power loss or harsh conditions.

A defense-related process program and Microchip manufacturing agreement could advance qualified domestic supply and a second source. Its small scale and Avalanche litigation remain risks.

423.title: ORCL / NBIS — Manchurius Hao
423.body:
Oracle long-dated options look attractive without requiring an extremely out-of-the-money strike.

Enthusiasm for Nebius recognizes the value of assembling GPUs, data centers, power, networks, contracts and delivery. Oracle has substantial resources in that same infrastructure business.

424.title: BTC — Manchurius Hao
424.body:
Repeatedly buying protective Bitcoin puts without assessing volatility pricing, skew or event timing can create a persistent premium expense.

Position sizing, cash and rebalancing should come before option hedges.

425.title: NBIS / PLTR — Ren
425.body:
Palantir named Nebius its preferred sovereign-AI infrastructure partner, creating a potential source of demand and distribution.

The integration would put Nebius compute and inference endpoints inside Palantir's perimeter, letting customers use open models on their data while retaining control of models, compute and data.

Corporate sovereignty requirements increasingly influenced deals. Modular data centers at sites with existing power offered faster deployment.

426.title: AEVA / SIVE.ST — Ren
426.body:
Aeva's entry into near-packaged and co-packaged optical sources could benefit Sivers as a potential laser supplier.

Serenity's analysis cited a joint development agreement with an optical-engine company, possible hyperscaler deployment in H2 2027 and a 2028 production ramp.

Sivers could supply continuous-wave DFB lasers and possibly amplifiers. Aeva was the only one of five contemplated earnings plays with a positive initial reaction.

427.title: ASTS — Ren
427.body: A convincing weekly close above $92 would confirm AST SpaceMobile's third-flag breakout, with resistance at $96-$97. Buying weakness toward $74-$75 was preferred amid macro volatility. A SpaceX IPO could provide a sector catalyst.

428.title: AMD — Ren
428.body: AMD was up 150% from the March entry. Record data-center revenue of $5.38 billion, up 39%, supported its role in CPU orchestration alongside AI inference.

429.title: LPK.DE — Ren
429.body:
LPKF's lasers could become a standard way to drill chip-packaging connections through glass without cracking it.

Over 80% of major industry participants reportedly chose its equipment for testing. Initial production-tool orders arrived in Q1 2026; large-scale production is expected in 2027. Shares remain held after gains of 335% from the January purchase and 130% since doubling the position in April.

430.title: PDFS — Ren
430.body:
PDF Solutions remains held for faster H2 growth from testing equipment and chip-analysis software.

Q1 sales rose 26% to $60.1m, but fell from $62.4m in Q4; backlog dropped to $246m from $254m. A pullback is possible.

One eProbe should earn Q2 revenue, with five more 2026 shipments targeted and Exensio AI beta in Q3. Annual growth guidance stays 20%. Q1 adjusted operating margin was 25%; 27% operating and 77% gross margins are longer-term targets.

431.title: CRDO — Ren
431.body:
Credo looks attractive for a trade after a roughly 20% earnings fall, not as a preferred 2030 holding. Interest begins below $160; $140 is especially attractive but may not be reached.

At $165 it is about 12x forward sales, versus 10x at $140, against over-85% growth and 68% gross-margin guidance. H2 slowing, customer concentration and potential optical replacement of cables from 2027 limit long-term appeal. BofA cut its target to $275 from $340, retaining Buy.

432.title: META — Jerry Capital
432.body:
Reported gains include 10% more time on Instagram Reels, 8% more Facebook video time and 9% more Facebook watch time in the U.S. and Canada.

Conversions rose 6% from GEM/Lattice and 1.6% from adaptive ranking. Continued improvements would support further investment in recommendations.

433.title: META — Q-Cap
433.body: Earning even a small amount from a fraction of Meta's 3.6 billion users could add meaningful revenue and help pay for AI investment.

434.title: AXTI — Traderstewie
434.body: AXT formed an inside-day candle within a falling wedge after a roughly 40% pullback over six days. Short-term oversold conditions offered a possible multiday rebound, targeting $55 and $60.

435.title: ONDS — mon
435.body: Ondas is growing revenue and orders and has raised its outlook. Acquisitions dilute shareholders in the near term; integrating those businesses and gaining scale could improve profitability over time.

436.title: IREN — mon
436.body:
IREN could grow tenfold long term if it stays independent. Power and land can serve multiple chip generations.

The proposed cycle is to sign customers, fund chips with deposits and equipment loans, then reinvest cash in expansion. At an assumed $20m annual revenue per MW, 1GW would earn $20bn a year, or $400bn over 20 years before costs and repeated chip replacement. This is a revenue scenario, not a profit forecast.

437.title: NOK — mon
437.body:
Nokia can sell more networking and optical equipment as AI data centers expand. Sustained demand and successful deliveries could double the shares over a year.

CEO Justin Hotard's computing background and the reported Nvidia investment and partnership help Nokia move beyond traditional telecom.

438.title: AAOI — mon
438.body:
AAOI has qualified lasers and demand, but limited capacity constrains transceiver and chip-adjacent optics sales.

Management expects monthly 800G/1.6T capacity to rise from nearly 200,000 units to about 650,000 by end-2026 and over 930,000 by end-2027. High-volume lasers for optics placed near network chips should matter more around late Q3 2027. Customer concentration, spending and valuation make delivery essential.

439.title: SPCX — mon
439.body:
The preference is to stay out while previously restricted SpaceX shares become eligible for sale.

The concern is potential selling from employees and early investors, not new-share dilution. A collapse is not assumed; the test is how well buyers absorb the available supply.

440.title: HIMS — mon
440.body:
Hims could keep patients longer by connecting their tests, treatments and ongoing care.

More subscribers would make the service more attractive to drugmakers, while additional services could increase spending per customer.

The opportunity still depends on responsible medical care, regulatory compliance and successful expansion abroad.

441.title: COIN — Manchurius Hao
441.body: Further progress on the CLARITY Act could benefit Coinbase because its compliant platform can connect users and institutions to crypto, derivatives, tokenized assets, stablecoins and stock exposure.

442.title: 000660.KS — Art of Speculation
442.body: SK Hynix is the preferred memory stock because of its high-bandwidth memory business and key customer relationships. Supply is still expected to remain tight.

443.title: IREN / SKHY — mon
443.body:
IREN and SK hynix could benefit as AI labs spend more on compute infrastructure.

Capital raised by Anthropic and other AI companies is expected to flow into GPUs, memory, data centers, networking and power because compute remains the bottleneck.

444.title: AAPL / SNAP — mon
444.body:
Apple buying Snap's Specs business could accelerate Apple's entry into smart glasses while ending Snap's prolonged development spending.

Snap contributes the glasses technology. Apple contributes devices, software, services and distribution that could bring it to more customers. No deal has been announced.

445.title: HOOD / SOFI — mon
445.body:
Robinhood's faster product expansion helps explain why its shares have outperformed SoFi since their 2021 listings.

SoFi still has record revenue, a bank charter and 38% growth. The gap is that Robinhood keeps launching products and entering new businesses.
